data.title: VHS, VCDs, and Laserdiscs in Southeast Asia
data.author: mikece
data.article_summary: 在东南亚，VCD和激光影碟（Laserdiscs）比VHS磁带更受欢迎，主要原因是热带气候导致的磁带发霉问题。VHS磁带在潮湿环境下容易长霉，影响播放质量，而本地购买的磁带则较少出现这种问题。此外，进口磁带还可能出现卡带问题，使得人们更青睐光盘格式。尽管VHS在新加坡等地区使用广泛，但光盘格式如激光影碟因其较长的使用寿命和较好的质量，受到影音爱好者和租赁店的欢迎。然而，由于价格较高，VCD（Video CD）在1990年代成为更大众化的选择，使用与音乐CD相同的标准，价格更亲民，因而广泛流行。

主要讨论点：各种视频格式和物理媒体的发展、使用及其相关文化

不同观点：
• **prmoustache**：认为SVCD在DVD普及之前提供了接近DVD质量的体验，并且由于其兼容性强和成本低，曾是一个具有吸引力的选择。可以通过使用两张CDR来提高质量，且成本仍低于DVDR。
• **xxr**：质疑Laserdisc相较于磁带的防潮优势，指出Laserdisc也存在LaserRot（分层/腐蚀）问题，尽管磁带的湿度问题可能更严重。
• **Scoundreller**：提到跨国或跨州观看相同电视节目并不容易，尤其是对于直播电视，通常需要依赖盗版。
• **maxglute**：分享了在北京发现VCD商店的经历，这些VCD不仅重新包装成类似精装收藏品，还提供个性化服务，如自定义颜色。
• **TrackerFF**：惊讶于在非西方国家看到大量盗版磁带和DVD在普通商店出售，这在他原本的预期之外。
• **magnio**：指出文章中对VCD的缩写解释存在不一致，先解释了全称但后来只用缩写，造成混淆。
• **2muchcoffeeman**：回忆了使用VHS清洁器的方法，通过酒精和快进倒带清洁磁带。
• **esafak**：对Laserdisc在西方国家的稀有性和高生产成本提出疑问，并询问谁制造了这些设备。
• **jnaina**：回忆了80年代新加坡某些店铺中出售的VHS盗版和成人内容，这些商品在特定地方可以找到。
• **aspenmayer**：提到自己拥有一个可能是盗版的SVCD，但包装精美，难以分辨真伪，并联想到VHS和Laserdisc的时代。
• **OneFriend2575**：认为VCD在东南亚不仅是格式，更是VHS盗版和早期DVD之间的桥梁，特别提到由于官方发布时间延迟，导致盗版市场繁荣。
• **naravara**：遗憾于媒体格式从VCD/CD演变到DVD和Blu-ray时没有选择Laserdisc的大小，认为大尺寸的物理媒体更适合收藏者，并且可以避免高密度压缩。

44533759.article_content:
VHS, VCDs, and Laserdiscs in Southeast Asia
Friday 11 July 2025
One of those factoids you often hear about Southeast Asia is that VCDs and Laserdiscs were more popular than VHS tapes. The cited reason is usually mould, on account of their tropical climates. But there was more to it.
For starters, what are VCDs and Laserdiscs? One of them is an initialism, and the other one is a word that sometimes employs camelCase. Initialisms are distinct from acronyms, in that you don’t pronounce them as a word. Laser is an acronym, and ATM is an initialism. camelCased words are so-named because the uppercase letter midway through a word bears a resemblance to the named animal and its distinctive hump.
I remember at UniSA I had a lecturer who insisted our variables and class definitions
useCamelCase
, and another lecturer
insisted_on_underscores
. Remembering which person wanted what was a constant struggle, especially when I’d have NetBeans open and I’d be working on both assignments simultaneously.
NetBeans is also camelCase!
Where was I going with this?
Tapes in Singapore
VHS tapes were everywhere when I was a kid in Australia. Much like the US, it was how our parents handled “time shifting”, which was a fancy term meaning “skip ads and watch stuff later”. My parents would receive care packages from recorded Australian TV when we moved to Singapore, at least until we got
The Australia Network
on cable. It’s wild to me to think people can simply move overseas and interstate now and watch the same intertube programming, but that’s a different post.
VHS was definitely used in Singapore. You could walk into Sim Lim Square or a
Best Denki
and get your tapes alongside cassettes for your Walkmans. They came in all the same formulations and lengths as what you get overseas. I had local friends who’s parents had
walls
of the stuff, much as mine did. I remember being fascinated by the carts with traditional Chinese spines from Taiwan, mixed in with handwritten notes about English shows.
VHS tapes were also
significantly
cheaper than back in Australia, presumably in part because they were made locally, or at least geographically closer. Heck, I even saw Betamax tapes for sale, despite the heyday for the format predating when I lived there.
Fun fact
as those YouTubers say, Singapore was once the largest manufacturer of floppy disk drives! Not bad for a country smaller than most Australian farms. But I digress, again.
Hot fuzz
While VHS was used, it wasn’t as popular as optical formats.
The factoid about mould is correct: Singapore’s tropical climate did cause mould issues on tapes. Tapes we imported from Australia would develop a nasty white fuzz that would appear behind those transparent reel windows. I don’t remember it ever causing issues during playback, though we had a tale from a family friend who played a tape that was so gummed up it jammed the machine. Yuck! This spooked my parents sufficiently that they’d consign any tapes exhibiting the fuzz to ewaste; I guess they didn’t think it was worth attempting to clean them.
Curiously, tapes bought
locally
in Singapore didn’t exhibit the same moulding issues; or at least, to the same extent. I’m not sure if it was on account of them being physically newer, or maybe tape manufacturers updated their formulas to make them better resistant to mould growth.
You can see an example of an Australian tape that was subjected to Singaporean humidity over many years. One day I’ll get around to cleaning this, if and when I figure out how to.
Enter optical formats
This does partly explain the popularity of optical formats over magnetic tape in Singapore, and in other affluent parts of Asia like Hong Kong and Kuala Lumpur. Laserdiscs were one of these formats, which were popular in video rental stores much as VHS was in the West. The Laserdisc you saw at the start of this post was an ex-rental, as you can see from this old Singapore government certificate:
Wikipedia summarises this advantage
, along with economic reasons for the format’s relative success:
Laserdiscs were also popular alternatives to videocassettes among movie enthusiasts in the more affluent regions of South East Asia, such as Singapore, due to their high integration with the Japanese export market and the disc-based media’s superior longevity compared to videocassette, especially in the humid conditions endemic to that area of the world.
There’s a “citation needed” link in the article, but this jibes with my experience. Singaporeans were becoming wealthy during this time, and they bought a
lot
of Japanese goods.
The mighty (small) VCD
While Laserdiscs were popular among videophiles and rental stores, their cost was still prohibitive for most people. Rather than going down the route of tape though, Video CDs became the dominant format in the 1990s for video distribution.

data.title: Show HN: We made our own inference engine for Apple Silicon
data.author: darkolorin
data.article_summary: "uzu" 是一个高性能的AI模型推理引擎，专为Apple Silicon设计，具有以下特点：简单的高层API、混合架构（支持GPU和MPSGraph计算）、统一的模型配置、可追溯的计算以确保正确性，以及利用Apple设备的统一内存。它提供了Rust接口和Swift绑定，支持通过CLI运行和服务器模式。使用者可以通过Cargo添加依赖并编写代码进行模型推理，也可以通过提供的脚本下载预处理模型。该项目采用MIT许可证，由Rust和Metal开发，适用于大规模语言模型的推理任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕推理引擎（inference engine）的速度、性能、兼容性、技术选型等方面的讨论，特别关注其在Mac上的表现及与其它推理引擎的比较。

不同观点：
• [giancarlostoro] 认为Nvidia在AI领域的优势使得其硬件成为必须选择，但同时好奇该推理引擎在AMD或Intel GPU上的表现，并希望了解模型的通用性。
• [zackangelo] 分享了他们使用Rust编写推理引擎的经验，并提到使用了ndarray和mpsgraph，而他们选择了candle。
• [khurs] 关注该引擎是否已经添加到HomeBrew等包管理器中，并强调跨平台（Mac到Linux/容器）的一致性。
• [homarp] 对引擎支持的量化类型感兴趣，并询问在特定模型上使用该引擎是否会更快。
• [floam] 将该引擎与Anemll进行比较，提出了性能和功能上的潜在竞争。
• [smpanaro] 质疑在实际应用中Apple的神经引擎（ANE）的使用频率，并认为优化速度通常倾向于使用GPU。
• [ewuhic] 关心项目的长期发展路线图，并将其与llama cpp的成功进行对比。
• [zdw] 对该引擎与MLX的性能比较感兴趣。
• [rnxrx] 对Qwen模型相对于Llama模型的性能提升原因感到好奇。
• [skybrian] 询问基准测试结果的单位，以确认数值越高是否代表性能越好。
• [dcreater] 认为该项目在小模型上有一定的速度提升，但质疑其整体目标和社区采用潜力。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现上，Rust被多次提及，[TheMagicHorsey] 讨论了Rust的复杂性及其学习曲线，与C和Zig进行了比较。
• 项目命名上，[greggh] 提到了“Mirai”这个词可能让人联想到负面的物联网DDoS事件，暗示命名可能需要更谨慎。
• 讨论中多次出现对不同推理引擎（如llama cpp、Anemll、MLX等）的比较，显示出社区对性能和适用性的高度关注。
• 争议焦点在于该推理引擎的实际性能优势和应用场景，特别是在与Nvidia和GPU的比较中，部分评论者对其通用性和必要性持怀疑态度。

uzu
A high-performance inference engine for AI models on Apple Silicon. Key features:
Simple, high-level API
Hybrid architecture
, where layers can be computed as GPU kernels or via MPSGraph (a low-level API beneath CoreML with
ANE
access)
Unified model configurations, making it easy to add support for new models
Traceable computations to ensure correctness against the source-of-truth implementation
Utilizes unified memory on Apple devices

Overview
For a detailed explanation of the architecture, please refer to the
documentation
.
Models
uzu
uses its own model format. To export a specific model, use
lalamo
. First, get the list of supported models:
uv run lalamo list-models
Then, export the specific one:
uv run lalamo convert meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct --precision float16
Alternatively, you can download a preprepared model using the sample script:
./scripts/download_test_model.sh
$MODEL_PATH

“English Translators of Homer” by Simeon Underwood
July 12, 2025
Leave a comment
I must caveat the rest of my remarks by saying I believe the book I was looking for would be titled “English Translations of Homer” rather than “English Translators of Homer.” This book is a history of the translators, the choices they made in translation, and how they were influenced by previous translations and by the style and culture of their times. Whereas, what I was looking for would spend more time comparing the texts. That said, I think the author made a mistake by not illustrating more of his points with quotations from the texts. It gets frustrating to be told about Pope’s style, or Rieu’s choice of prose over verse, and go for pages without an example passage. I actually checked a version of Rieu out of the library while reading this book, so I could see what the author was talking about. Of course, that would be a longer book, but at 68 pages, this provides excessively short coverage of a large topic. At twice the length, it would still be a mere outline.
With those remarks aside, this is a good book. It really clarified how to think about the various translations and what I am looking for when I read them. Underwood starts by saying every act of translation is a balance between preserving the source text and producing a readable and enjoyable target text. This is particularly challenging in the case of poetry, where the choice and organization of the words is as or more important than their meaning. In fact, it is easy to imagine that in some cases this task may be impossible: hypothetically, there may not exist the words in English to translate a Haiku while maintaining the 5-7-5 form.
A particular challenge with Homer is that these texts are fundamental historic documents: not meaning they are histories, but rather that the texts appear at the very beginning of Western history. It is very reasonable to want to read them as close to the original Greek as possible to understand not only the events they describe (whatever their historical authenticity) but also the evolution of language and poetry, and to glimpse the mind and times of the author(s).
On the other hand, Iliad and Odyssey are both enjoyable and interesting as stories, and it is reasonable to want to produce a text that emphasizes that. And here comes yet another challenge beyond even translating contemporary poetry. Is the text supposed to capture the experience of a reader (or listener) from ancient times by, for example, using ancient idioms and similes, or create an analogous mood in the modern reader by updating those constructs?
For example, in Book 5, the hero Diomedes wounds Aphrodite. The love goddess retreats to Olympus, where she complains to Zeus. Lattimore’s translation goes:
“Tydeus’ son Diomedes, the too high-hearted, stabbed me as I was carrying my own beloved son out of the fighting, Aineias, who beyond all else in the world is dear to me; so now this is no horrible war of Achaians and Trojans, but the Danaäns are beginning to fight even with the immortals.”
Christopher Logue’s highly stylized and modernized version reads:
Love: ‘Father, see this.’ (Her wrist.) ‘Human strikes god! Communism! The end of everything!’
The modern reader, who presumably does not honor the gods or understand the context of words like Achaians and Danaans, may feel something closer to the emotional intent of the poet in Logue’s version, even though the words themselves would make no sense to Homer.
(The above illustrates a problem with this book, which is almost devoid of side-by-side comparisons to explain the author’s points. I had to find my own examples, which may or may not actually match Underwood’s intent.)
I found the middle chapters of the book, focused on Chapman, Pope, and Rieu, quite dull for the reasons already mentioned (telling rather than showing the choices made by these translators). Fortunately, the final chapter is about Christopher Logue’s controversial “account” of the Iliad, “War Music.” Logue is literally not a translator, and does not claim to be. He worked from English rather than Greek texts: the language was translated for him.  And he writes in a distinctly modern style, one that would be controversial and a matter of taste in any age, including today’s. Choosing Logue’s approach highlights the translation choices Underwood started this book with.
Here’s Logue (as quoted by Underwood) talking about versions that emphasize the source text:
I look at new translations as they come out, that of Professors Knox and Fagle, for example, which is a touch sharper than Professor Lattimore’s. However, these professors may have been reading Homer all their lives, but he’s failed to teach them what verse is.
Ouch! Suddenly, Bernard Knox’s criticism of Logue

data.title: NIST ion clock sets new record for most accurate clock
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）的研究人员开发出世界上最精确的原子钟，能够将时间测量到小数点后19位。这一“量子逻辑钟”依靠量子计算技术，将带电的铝离子与镁离子配对，经过20年的持续改进，其精度比之前的记录高出41%，稳定性是其他离子钟的2.6倍。该钟的精度和稳定性得益于对每个组件的精心改进，包括激光、离子阱和真空室。铝离子钟的“滴答”频率极其稳定，受环境条件影响小，但由于铝离子难以用激光探测和冷却，研究团队通过镁离子辅助冷却和读数，实现了精确测量。该成果发表在《物理评论快报》上，有助于重新定义秒并推动科学和技术进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：原子钟的精确性和应用

不同观点：
• [herrmaier] 认为制作出极其精确的钟表是一种炫耀资本，尤其是在家庭聚会中借此展示自己的工作成就。
• [mikewarot] 强调了这些高精度钟表的实际影响，例如通过测量重力引起的时间膨胀来检测微小的高度差异。他还提到目前市面上可以买到的相对便宜的原子钟。
• [frankfrank13] 提到了与NOAA和NIST相关的个人经历，并指出该机构面临的预算风险，提供了一个相关新闻链接。
• [infogulch] 引用了有关原子钟的近期讨论，并提到一种基于原子核的新型时钟，可能比现有的电子轨道时钟更精确。
• [renlo] 和 [Babkock] 对如何测量最精确钟表的准确性提出了疑问，质疑如果所有钟表都有误差，该如何验证其准确性。
• [mlhpdx] 探讨了“钟表”与“时钟信号”的区别，类似于位置编码器的相对和绝对概念。

补充讨论：
• [user3939382] 指出这种精确钟表对GPS精度的影响，并提到其可能带来的应用，例如驾驶车道的界定。
• [perihelions] 提供了一篇预印本文章链接，该文章讨论了一种系统不确定性为 $5.5\times10^{-19}$ 的高稳定性单离子钟。
• [kridsdale3] 以幽默的方式建议让Hodinkee来报道此事。
• [tguvot] 提到通过美国邮政或传真机获取NIST NTP服务器认证的繁琐过程，并指出由于办公限制可能导致的延迟。
• [jasonthorsness] 评论文章质量好，并提到铝钟比铯钟更精确但使用难度大，目前已解决相关技术问题。
• [johnnyballgame] 以玩笑的方式问这种钟是否带有贪睡按钮。
• [gwerbret] 纠正了关于精确性和准确性之间的术语使用错误，强调精度不等于准确性。

NEWS
NIST Ion Clock Sets New Record for Most Accurate Clock in the World
July 14, 2025
Share
Facebook
Linkedin
X.com
Email
NIST researchers have made the most accurate atomic clock to date — one that can measure time down to the 19th decimal place.
This “quantum logic clock,” under continuous development for 20 years, relies on quantum computing techniques that pair an electrically charged aluminum atom (ion) with a magnesium ion.
This new result contributes to the international effort to define the second with a much greater level of accuracy than before, enabling new scientific and technological advances.
(From left to right) Mason Marshall, David Hume, Willa Arthur-Dworschack and Daniel Rodriguez Castillo stand in front of the aluminum ion clock at NIST. With its recent improvements, the clock can pave the way for the campaign to redefine the second as well as explore new ideas in physics.
Credit:
R. Jacobson/NIST
There’s a new record holder for the most accurate clock in the world. Researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have improved their
atomic clock
based on a trapped aluminum ion. Part of the latest wave of
optical atomic clocks
, it can perform timekeeping with 19 decimal places of accuracy.
Optical clocks are typically evaluated on two levels — accuracy (how close a clock comes to measuring the ideal “true” time, also known as systematic uncertainty) and stability (how efficiently a clock can measure time, related to statistical uncertainty). This new record in accuracy comes out of 20 years of continuous improvement of the aluminum ion clock. Beyond its world-best accuracy, 41% greater than the previous record, this new clock is also 2.6 times more stable than any other ion clock. Reaching these levels has meant carefully improving every aspect of the clock, from the laser to the trap and the vacuum chamber.
The team published its results in
Physical Review Letters
.
“It’s exciting to work on the most accurate clock ever,” said Mason Marshall, NIST researcher and first author on the paper. “At NIST we get to carry out these long-term plans in precision measurement that can push the field of physics and our understanding of the world around us.”
NIST physicist David Hume holds the newly modified ion trap for the aluminum ion clock. By modifying the trap, the aluminum ion and its magnesium ion partner were able to “tick” unperturbed.
Credit:
R. Jacobson/NIST
The aluminum ion makes an exceptionally good clock, with an extremely steady, high-frequency “ticking” rate. Its ticks are more stable than those of cesium, which provides the
current scientific definition
of the second, said David Hume, the NIST physicist leading the aluminum ion clock project. And the aluminum ion isn’t as sensitive to some environmental conditions, like temperature and magnetic fields.
But the aluminum ion is kind of shy, Marshall explained. Aluminum is difficult to probe and cool with lasers, both necessary techniques for atomic clocks. The research group therefore paired the aluminum ion with magnesium. Magnesium doesn’t have the beautiful ticking properties of aluminum, but it can be easily controlled with lasers. “This ‘buddy system’ for ions is called quantum logic spectroscopy,” said Willa Arthur-Dworschack, a graduate student on the project. The magnesium ion cools the aluminum ion, slowing it down. It also moves in tandem with its aluminum partner, and the state of the clock can be read out via the magnesium ion’s motion, making this a “quantum logic” clock. Even with this coordination, there was still an array of physical effects to characterize, said Daniel Rodriguez Castillo, also a graduate student on the project.
“It’s a big, complex challenge, because every part of the clock’s design affects the clock,” Rodriguez Castillo said.
One challenge was the design of the trap where the ions are held, which was causing tiny movements of the ions, called excess micromotion, that were lowering the clock’s accuracy. That excess micromotion throws off the ions’ tick rate. Electrical imbalances at opposite sides of the trap were creating extra fields that disturbed the ions. The team redesigned the trap, putting it on a thicker diamond wafer and modifying the gold coatings on the electrodes to fix the imbalance of the electric field. They also made the gold coatings thicker to reduce resistance. Refining the trap this way slowed the ions’ motion and let them “tick” unperturbed.

data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者在探索机器人表现力和互动性方面的实验过程，特别是通过构建名为Shoggoth Mini的软体机器人。最初，作者受到Apple的ELEGNT论文和SpiRobs的启发，开始研究如何让机器人更具表现力。在硬件设计中，作者意外地通过使用不同颜色的3D打印材料和简单的绘画面部特征，创造了一个既可爱又略带诡异的机器人外观。在解决了一系列技术问题后，如电缆缠绕和校准，作者成功设计出一个可以通过触控板直观控制的机器人 tentacle。该系统的控制分为低层级的开环和闭环策略，并通过简单的2D到3D映射实现自动控制。最终，Shoggoth Mini成为了一个探索机器人表现力的实验平台，展示了如何通过意外发现和迭代改进设计出更自然的机器人互动。

主要讨论点：关于机器人设计、人工智能的表达性与生命感、以及机器人应用的多元观点

不同观点：
• **关于机器人的生命感与可预测性**：
  - **rainingmonkey** 指出，虽然机器人表现力丰富，但随着用户逐渐理解其运作机制，机器人变得不再像有生命。表达性与生命感的区别在于不可预测性和一定的模糊性。他质疑是否应制造感觉上“有生命”的机器人，或者是否有一个界限，超过这个界限，机器人会因为过于不可预测而让人不安。

• **关于机器人响应速度与技术实现的讨论**：
  - **dylan604** 提到了机器人响应延迟的问题，认为GPT处理的延迟让人感到不安，甚至比新闻采访中的延迟更糟。他建议通过LED等视觉提示来缓解这种不适感，并指出由于GPT的云端处理，延迟问题可能难以避免。

• **关于机器人设计的创新性与应用**：
  - **SequoiaHope** 对机器人（尤其是“连续体机器人”）在医疗领域的应用表示赞赏，并分享了一个相关讲座视频，显示出对机器人科研价值的肯定。
  - **typs** 则批评当前机器人设计过于集中在人形机器人上，表达了对更多样化设计（如蜘蛛/乌贼混合型机器人）的期望。

• **关于机器人外观设计的美学与伦理问题**：
  - **zhyder** 表示欣赏这种不模仿自然生物的机器人设计，担心未来可能难以区分自然与机器人。他希望未来机器人能保持明显的人造特征。
  - **sparrish** 持反对意见，直接拒绝这种设计，并通过电影《异形》中的“抱脸虫”形象表达对这种设计的恐惧。

• **关于机器人项目的惊叹与文化联想**：
  - **alex_suzuki** 和 **dvngnt_** 对该项目的创意和个人项目的水平表示赞叹，后者还提到日本媒体中类似机器人的趋势，暗示了对文化影响的关注。
  - **ge96** 和 **KaoruAoiShiho** 则分别联想到了《蜘蛛侠》中的“章鱼博士”和相关角色，显示出对科幻角色与现实科技结合的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• **关于机器人技术专利与科研背景**：
  - **dcre** 和 **regularfry** 提到了Spirobs项目背后的科研论文和专利问题，显示出对技术创新与知识产权的关注。

• **关于机器人应用于玩具和教育的潜力**：
  - **tsunamifury** 提出了将这种技术应用于玩具（如通过基本互动和教育功能改变传统玩具）的想法，强调了这种技术在玩具行业的潜在变革性。

争议焦点：
- **机器人的生命感与不可预测性**：rainingmonkey提出的机器人是否应感觉“有生命”的问题引发了对生命感、不可预测性和人机舒适度的讨论。

44572377.article_content:
Over the past year, robotics has been catching up with the LLM era. Pi’s π0.5
can clean unseen homes
. Tesla’s Optimus can follow
natural language cooking instructions
. These systems are extremely impressive, but they feel stuck in a utilitarian mindset of robotic appliances. For these future robots to live with us, they must be expressive. Expressiveness communicates internal state such as intent, attention, and confidence. Beyond its functional utility as a communication channel, expressiveness makes interactions feel natural. Without it, you get the textbook
uncanny valley
effect.
Earlier this year, I came across Apple’s
ELEGNT
paper, which frames this idea rigorously through a Pixar-like lamp to show how posture and timing alone can convey intention. Around the same time, I discovered
SpiRobs
, a soft tentacle robot that feels oddly alive with just simple movements. One system was carefully designed to express intent while the other just moved, yet somehow felt like it had intent. That difference was interesting. I started building Shoggoth Mini as a way to explore it more directly. Not with a clear goal, but to see what would happen if I pushed embodiment into stranger territory. This post retraces that process, the happy accidents, and what I learned about building robots.
ELEGNT
SpiRobs
SpiRobs demo
Hardware
The first challenge was creating a testbed to explore the control of SpiRobs. I started very simple: a plate to hold three motors, and a dome to lift the tentacle above them. This setup wasn’t meant to be the final design, only a platform for quick experimentation. However, halfway through 3D printing, I ran out of black filament and had to finish the dome in grey. This made it look like the dome had a mouth. When my flatmate saw it sitting on my desk, he grabbed a marker and drew some eyes. It looked good: cute, weird, slightly unsettling. I used ChatGPT to explore renders, and decided that this accident would become the form factor.
Later, I mounted stereo cameras on the dome to track the tentacle. Robot eyes are eerie. You keep expecting movement, but nothing ever happens. That prediction error
focuses attention even more
.
The original open-spool design relied on constant cable tension, but any slight perturbation (such as testing a buggy new policy) would make the cables leave the spool and tangle around the motor shafts. The process to fix it required untying the knot at the tip holding the cables together, and dismantling the whole robot. Adding simple spool covers eliminated most tangles and made iteration dramatically faster.
Another key step was adding a calibration script and pre-rolling extra wire length. This made it possible to:
Unroll and reroll the cables to open the robot without having to untie the tip knot, speeding up iteration dramatically
Calibrate cable tension precisely and as often as needed
Give control policies slack to work with during motion
Rolling the cables back after working on Shoggoth Mini's insides
Finally, as you can see in the video, the standard 3-cable SpiRobs design sags under its own weight. This makes consistent behavior hard to reproduce. I had to thicken the spine just enough to prevent sag, but not so much that it would deform permanently under high load.
You can explore the current CAD assembly here, with all STL files for 3D printing included in the
repo
.
This is an interactive 3D model - click and drag to rotate, scroll to zoom
Manual control
With the hardware ready, the next step was to feel how the tentacle moved. To simplify control, I reduced the tentacle’s three tendon lengths (a 3D space) down to two intuitive dimensions you can manipulate with a trackpad.
Concretely, each of the three tendons has a principal pulling direction in the 2D plane, forming a triangular basis that sums to zero. By projecting the 2D cursor control vector onto each tendon’s principal axis, you compute how much each tendon should shorten or lengthen to align with the desired direction.
This projection is linear:
$$
s_i = \mathbf{v}_i^\top \mathbf{c}
$$
where:
$\mathbf{c}$ is the 2D cursor vector,
$\mathbf{v}_i$ is the principal axis of tendon $i$.
Positive $s_i$ means shortening the tendon; negative means lengthening it. In practice, the cursor input is normalized to keep the motor commands in a reasonable range.
While this 2D mapping doesn’t expose the tentacle’s full configuration space (there are internal shapes it cannot reach), it is intuitive. Anyone can immediately move the tentacle by dragging on a trackpad, seeing the tip follow the cursor in the same direction.
Unexpectedly, this simple 2D-to-3D mapping became the backbone of the entire system. Later, all automated control policies, from hardcoded primitives to reinforcement learning, reused the same projection layer to output actions.
Trackpad control
System design
The system has two control layers. Low-level control uses both open-loop primitives (like “<yes>” or “<shake>”) and closed-loop RL policies (l

data.title: Designing for the Eye: Optical corrections in architecture and typography
data.author: ArmageddonIt
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了建筑和字体设计中的光学修正（或光学调整），强调视觉设计需考虑光学错觉。文章以Müller-Lyer错觉为例，说明两条等长线因箭头方向不同而看似长度不一，这种错觉不受文化背景限制，甚至在动物界也能观察到。作者提到，视觉艺术家、字体设计师等应依赖眼睛的判断，而非单纯依靠测量。文中引用了Paul Renner的《The Art of Typography》一书，指出对于艺术家而言，没有光学错觉，他们从一开始就考虑了表象形式，并根据视觉印象工作。最终，当视觉印象与测量冲突时，应优先考虑视觉印象。

主要讨论点：设计与美学在不同领域（科技、建筑、字体、音乐、logo设计等）中的体现和争议

不同观点：
• 关于微软设计的评价：
  - [1970-01-01] 认为微软以前的Windows和Office具有" brutalist beauty "，可以高度自定义，而如今的O365和Azure设计则像是对其 former design 的讽刺。
  - 反对观点隐含在[soperj]的评论中，指出微软的设计缺乏原创性，甚至抄袭了Xerox Parc和Braun的设计理念，批评其"没有品味"。

• 关于知识内化与技术依赖的讨论：
  - [anactofgod] 认为互联网和AI使得人们不再重视自身知识的积累，强调只有当知识内化于心时，才能产生新的见解。
  - 该观点未在其他评论中直接回应，但隐含了对技术进步（如AI）影响传统认知方式的质疑。

• 关于HDR和图像处理技术的讨论：
  - [Lu2025] 提出iPhone 16的HDR照片显得“overprocessed”和“cartoonish”，尽管技术上更接近人眼的动态范围，但视觉上感觉不自然。
  - 没有直接反对意见，但该评论指出了现代图像技术在追求真实感时可能带来的不适。

• 关于建筑与字体设计中的光学平衡：
  - [necovek] 强调现代建筑和字体设计忽视了光学平衡，认为这是美观的重要因素，并通过帕特农神庙柱子的设计为例说明。
  - 该观点未受到直接反驳，反而通过[bitwize]的评论得到了支持，后者通过LilyPond音乐排版中的不对称美化细节进一步论证了设计中的光学调整。

• 关于Taj Mahal设计的讨论：
  - [zeckalpha] 指出Taj Mahal并非方形设计，使其看起来像是正方形，这是一个未被提及但值得注意的设计细节。
  - 该评论未引发争议，只是作为一个补充的设计例子。

• 关于字体设计在HN上受欢迎程度的讨论：
  - [pcrh] 对字体设计在Hacker News上受欢迎表示好奇，认为其受欢迎程度高于其他设计形式。
  - 该观点未引发直接讨论，但隐含了对设计社区兴趣点的观察。

• 关于logo设计的实用建议：
  - [taneq] 提供了关于logo设计的建议，强调logo应尽量适应盒子形状，保持重心稳定，并避免不对称设计以免布局不协调。
  - 该观点未受到直接反驳，更多是作为实用设计技巧分享。

• 关于哥特式建筑与字体演化的讨论：
  - [hoseja] 解释了哥特式建筑与当时书写风格的演化关系，指出并非有意对应，而是工具和技术限制下的自然演化。
  - 该评论未引发直接争议，但提供了对历史设计演化的另一种解释。

补充讨论：
- 设计美学在不同领域（科技产品、建筑、字体、音乐等）中的共通性与差异性。
- 技术进步（如HDR、AI）对传统设计理念的冲击与适应。
- 设计中的光学平衡与不对称调整在不同设计领域中的重要性。
- 历史设计演化与现代设计理念的对比与反思。

争议焦点：
- 微软设计的评价与技术抄袭争议。
- 知识内化与技术依赖之间的平衡。
- 现代技术追求真实感与传统视觉审美之间的矛盾。

Designing for the Eye
Optical Corrections in Architecture and Typography
By Niko Kitsakis, June 2025
This article highlights a special aspect of both visual design and architecture: Optical cor­rections (or optical ad­just­ments, if you prefer). If you found
my piece about legible typefaces
interesting, youâll likely enjoy this one as well. Since I included many visual examples that are size-sensitive, make sure you read this on a big screen and not your mobile device.
Optical Illusions
The MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion, pictured below, makes you think that, of two lines, one is longer than the other when in fact they are of the same length. It appears in virtually every introductory book on graphic de­sign and, of course, in books on per­ception and psy­cho­lo­gy. You might not have known it by name, but you must have seen it before:
â
â
Is the blue line on top longer than the one at the bottom? Click the arrows to find out.
It used to be said that, in order to see the illu­sion, you must have grown up in an environ­ment where lines very similar to these would explicitly appear in your everyday surroundings â in architecture and furniture, for example, or when you had played with building blocks as a kid and so on. This is, incidentally, what I too was taught at my school of visual design some decades ago. However, I always had a hard time be­liev­ing it, and according to
some new research
, this is indeed not the case: Not only can the illu­sion be per­ceived by anyone, no matter their cultural background, it even extends (to some degree) to the animal kingdom and can be ex­pe­ri­enced in a haptic version as well.
The reason why I never really believed that the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion (and others like it) would work only on people who grew up in our Western culture is that, in the first place, it seems visually far too uni­ver­sal to begin with. After all, theyâre just lines. You can draw them in the sand, and they can appear naturally in many circum­stan­ces. When I look at another person, my brain will assign certain values to the length of that personâs arms, legs, and torso, and memorise them as some variety of line as well. If the brain didnât do that, we would not be able to tell if a body or facial features were out of proportion. So in my view, something dis­cern­ible only by people from a specific culture would have to be far more elaborate than an optical illusion of just a few lines.
While that was only my personal gut-feeling, I soon dis­co­vered that other people had made similar obser­va­tions. One such time was when I first read Paul Rennerâs 1940 book
Die Kunst der Typo­grafie
(The Art of Typo­graphy). The book covers pretty much every­thing you need to know to become a typo­graph­er, in­clu­ding that you should not rely on mea­su­ring things but rather on what your own eyes tell you:
Der glaube an das ZÃ¤hlen und Messen verfÃ¼hrt in allen KÃ¼nsten zu den grÃ¶bsten Fehlern.
The belief in counting and measuring leads to the grossest errors in all the arts.
Renner happens to show the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion in his book and writes about what to make of it and other visual illusions like it. Take a look at this book spread first:
If you read books, you have an advantage.
If you look closely, you can see a version of the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion in the top right box of the left page. Renner describes every optical illu­sion on that page separately, but whatâs interesting is how he con­clu­des that section. He says that the following applies to all of the optical illusions:
FÃ¼r die Anschauungsweise des KÃ¼nstlers, des Schriftschneiders und des Typographen gibt es hier keine optischen TÃ¤uschungen, sie rechnen von vornherein mit den scheinbaren Formen; was scheinbar falsch ist, ist fÃ¼r sie falsch; und was scheinbar richtig ist, ist fÃ¼r sie richtig. Es handelt sich also nicht darum, ein genaues ZÃ¤hlen, Messen und Bauen durch ein unbestimmtes, schwankendes, willkÃ¼rliches GefÃ¼hl, das niemand nach­prÃ¼fen kann, zu ersetzen, sondern man soll einfach den wirklichen Augenschein, dessen Feststellung ein sehr geÃ¼btes Auge erfordert, als maÃgeblich anerkennen; er ist zwar âsubjektivâ, aber er ist, wie die Gelehrten sagen, âintersubjektiv gleichâ, also bei allen Menschen den gleichen TÃ¤uschungen unterworfen. Da alle bildende Kunst fÃ¼r den Augenschein arbeitet, so mÃ¼ssen wir ihm Ã¼berall dort recht geben, wo er mit der Zahl und der Messung in Widerspruch gerÃ¤t.

44573887.article_summary: 本文讨论了建筑和字体设计中的光学修正（或光学调整），强调视觉设计需考虑光学错觉。文章以Müller-Lyer错觉为例，说明两条等长线因箭头方向不同而看似长度不一，这种错觉不受文化背景限制，甚至在动物界也能观察到。作者提到，视觉艺术家、字体设计师等应依赖眼睛的判断，而非单纯依靠测量。文中引用了Paul Renner的《The Art of Typography》一书，指出对于艺术家而言，没有光学错觉，他们从一开始就考虑了表象形式，并根据视觉印象工作。最终，当视觉印象与测量冲突时，应优先考虑视觉印象。

data.title: Petabit-class transmission over > 1000 km using standard 19-core optical fiber
data.author: the_arun
data.article_summary: 2025年5月29日，日本信息通信研究机构（NICT）与住友电工株式会社合作，使用自主研发的19芯光纤实现了传输速率1.02 PB/s、传输距离1,808公里的世界纪录。该光纤具有标准包层直径0.125毫米，低损耗且兼容现有光纤基础设施。通过开发新型光放大中继技术，研究团队成功实现了超过1,000公里的长距离高容量传输，创下容量-距离积1.86 Ebits/s×km的纪录。这一成果标志着长距离、大容量光通信技术取得重大突破，为未来网络扩展和应对数据需求增长奠定了基础。研究结果已在第48届光纤通信会议（OFC 2025）上发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多芯光纤技术的现状、应用及其与传统技术的比较

不同观点：
• [throw0101c] 提到 NANOG 会议上有关光网络的常规演示，提供了一个详细介绍光网络技术的视频链接，展示了多芯光纤技术的背景和应用。

• [eqvinox] 指出文章中对19芯光纤被称为“标准”的描述不准确，实际并非标准光纤，而是由住友电工设计和制造的一种特定光纤。同时，他认为多芯光纤技术正在逐渐成熟。

• [exabrial] 提出疑问，比较了LAG组中的带宽聚合和多芯光纤中的带宽聚合方式，质疑为何在LAG中单个TCP流受限于单条链路速度，而多芯光纤可以实现整体更快的传输速度，并询问其中的技术差异。

• [aDfbrtVt] 认为该技术主要是一种高芯数弱耦合光纤的验证概念，并指出使用19通道MIMO接收结构在实际应用中是不切实际的，同时批评文章未提供MIMO增益的数据。

• [bcrl] 认为19芯光纤并非行业标准，指出电信行业中12芯光纤是黄金标准，且提到当前高芯数光缆使用更灵活的带状结构以提高密度，同时保持标准工具的兼容性。

• [Keyframe] 表示对光传输技术的兴趣，但更期待电气到光学的变革性转变，指出光传输的两端仍需电气转换，这会限制速度、消耗功率并产生热量，期待光学交换技术的突破。

补充讨论：
• [ksec] 提供了实际测试的数据，指出光纤传输距离的具体数值，并用美国地理宽度作为参考，帮助理解该技术的实际应用规模。

争议焦点：
• 多芯光纤是否可以称为“标准”光纤存在争议，[eqvinox] 和 [bcrl] 都指出了文章中描述的不准确性，强调19芯光纤并非行业标准。
• 对多芯光纤技术的实际应用可行性存在不同看法，[aDfbrtVt] 认为19通道MIMO结构不切实际，而 [eqvinox] 则认为多芯光纤技术正在成熟。
• [exabrial] 提出的LAG组带宽聚合与多芯光纤带宽聚合的技术差异问题，引发了对不同技术实现方式的讨论。

World Record Achieved in Transmission Capacity and Distance: With 19-core Optical Fiber with Standard Cladding Diameter 1,808 km Transmission of 1.02 Petabits per Second
- Expectation for Future Long-Distance High-Capacity Optical Communication Infrastructure -
May 29, 2025
(Japanese version released on April 24, 2025)
National Institute of Information and Communications Technology
Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd.
Highlights
The world's first successful petabit-class transmission over more than 1,000 km using standard 19-core optical fiber, achieving a transmission rate of 1.02 petabits per second over a distance of 1,808 km.
Achieved using a newly developed standard 19-core optical fiber, equivalent to 19 standard fibers, low loss across multiple wavelength bands, and the development of an optical amplification relay function compatible with this fiber.
This is a major step to realize future long-distance, large-capacity optical communication systems.
An
international research team
led by the Photonic Network Laboratory at the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT, President: TOKUDA Hideyuki Ph.D.), and including Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd. (Sumitomo Electric, President: INOUE Osamu) have set a new world record in optical fiber communications, achieving data transmission at 1.02
petabits
per second over a distance of 1,808 kilometers (roughly equivalent to the distance from Sapporo to Fukuoka, from Missouri to Montana or from Berlin to Naples). The experiment used a specially designed 19-core optical fiber with a
standard 0.125 mm cladding diameter
, compatible with existing fiber infrastructure. With a
capacity-distance product
of 1.86 exabits per second x km—the
highest ever recorded
—this demonstration marks the fastest long-distance transmission achieved in any optical fiber to date. The result represents a major step forward in developing scalable, high-capacity networks and addressing the world’s growing demand for data.
A standard cladding diameter 19-core optical fiber has been demonstrated to transmit more than 1 petabit per second in the past, but over relatively short distances, well below 1,000 km. The research team has achieved a dramatic extension of the transmission distance by developing a novel 19-core optical fiber also with a standard cladding diameter but with low loss across multiple wavelength bands used in commercial optical fiber transmission systems. In addition, an optical amplification system was developed to support the new optical fiber, which enabled a world record for long-distance high-capacity transmission. The newly developed technology is expected to make a significant contribution to both the expansion of the communication capacity and the long-range extension of optical communication infrastructure in the future, when communication demand increases.
The results of this experiment were accepted as a post-deadline paper presentation at the 48th Optical Fiber Communication Conference (OFC 2025) and presented on Thursday, April 3, 2025.

Research on new types of optical fibers and optical transmission systems that exceed the limits of conventional optical fiber transmission is being actively pursued around the world. An example of such fibers is
multi-core optical fibers

data.title: Mira Murati’s AI startup Thinking Machines valued at $12B in early-stage funding
data.author: spenvo
data.article_summary: Thinking Machines Lab，由前OpenAI高管Mira Murati创立的AI初创公司，近日宣布完成约20亿美元融资，估值达120亿美元。此轮融资由Andreessen Horowitz领投，Nvidia、Accel、ServiceNow等参投。尽管公司今年2月才成立，且尚未有收入或产品，但Murati成功吸引了大量投资。公司计划打造更安全、可靠的AI系统，其团队近三分之二为前OpenAI员工。Murati的离职和创立新公司反映了AI领域高管的争夺战，而投资者对AI初创企业的热情依然高涨，推动美国初创企业融资在2025年上半年激增。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Andreessen Horowitz（a16z）对Thinking Machines的大规模投资是否合理，以及对Thinking Machines的未来潜力的不同看法。

不同观点：
• 一些评论对a16z的投资持怀疑态度，认为这是在没有实际产品支持下的高风险赌博，并暗示可能依赖于未来可能的银行救助（bgwalter）。有人甚至将Thinking Machines比作科幻小说《沙丘》中的邪恶势力，表达了对其潜在威胁的担忧（oaiey）。

• 另一种观点认为，a16z的投资可能有其合理性，尽管外界看来可能是炒作。持这种观点的人认为，鉴于a16z过去的成功和失败，他们可能掌握了一些外界不了解的内情。这种观点倾向于保持乐观，并认为不应轻易否定这种大规模投资（erulabs）。

• 还有评论指出，市场对Thinking Machines的负面情绪可能过于激烈，特别是考虑到公司拥有来自OpenAI的顶尖人才，如Murati等（pdabbadabba）。有人支持这种观点，强调Thinking Machines拥有优秀的团队，如John Schulman等，值得期待（leesec）。

• 一种批评观点认为，a16z的行为类似于软银，通过短期信号操作市场，投资可能只是泡沫的一部分（malthaus）。还有人直言，VC们可能只是希望在这场AI竞赛中获得短期收益，并不真正关心长期发展（Runsthroughit）。

补充讨论：
• 有人调侃Thinking Machines可能在进行AI领域的“军备竞赛”，暗示高额投资可能用于打击竞争对手（dandanua）。

• 一些评论表达了对Thinking Machines具体产品的困惑和好奇，指出虽然公司吸引了大量顶尖人才，但尚未公开其具体项目（beauzero）。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于，a16z对Thinking Machines的大规模投资是否基于实际潜力，还是仅仅出于炒作和市场泡沫的考虑。不同评论者对AI领域高额投资的合理性以及未来前景持不同看法。

44573574.article_content:
July 15 (Reuters) - Thinking Machines Lab, the artificial intelligence startup founded by former OpenAI executive Mira Murati, said on Tuesday it has raised about $2 billion at a valuation of $12 billion in a funding round led by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.
The fundraise also saw participation from AI chip giant Nvidia
(NVDA.O)
, opens new tab
, Accel, ServiceNow
(NOW.N)
, opens new tab
, Cisco
(CSCO.O)
, opens new tab
, AMD
(AMD.O)
, opens new tab
and Jane Street, the startup said.
Sign up
here.
The massive funding round for a company launched only in February, with no revenue or products yet, underscores Murati's ability to attract investors in a sector where top executives have become coveted targets in an escalating talent war.
"We're excited that in the next couple months we will be able to share our first product, which will include a significant open source component and be useful for researchers and startups developing custom model," CEO Murati said in a
post
, opens new tab
on the X social media platform.
Reuters had
reported
in April Andreessen Horowitz was in talks to lead an outsized early-stage funding round.
Thinking Machines has said it wants to build artificial intelligence systems that are safer, more reliable and aimed at a broader number of applications than rivals. Nearly two-thirds of its team
at launch
comprised of former OpenAI employees.
Murati, who started Thinking Machines after an abrupt exit from OpenAI last September, is among a growing list of former executives from the ChatGPT maker who have launched AI startups.
Another two, Dario Amodei's Anthropic and Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence, have attracted former OpenAI researchers and raised billions of dollars in funding.
Investor enthusiasm toward new AI startups has stayed strong, despite some questions about tech industry spending.
That helped U.S. startup
funding surge nearly 76%
to $162.8 billion in the first half of 2025, with AI accounting for about 64.1% of the total deal value, according to a Pitchbook report.
Reporting by Krystal Hu in New York and Aditya Soni in Bengaluru; Editing by Anil D'Silva and Arun Koyyur

不同观点：
• 一些评论对a16z的投资持怀疑态度，认为这是在没有实际产品支持下的高风险赌博，并暗示可能依赖于未来可能的银行救助（bgwalter）。有人甚至将Thinking Machines比作科幻小说《沙丘》中的邪恶势力，表达了对其潜在威胁的担忧（oaiey）。

• 另一种观点认为，a16z的投资可能有其合理性，尽管外界看来可能是炒作。持这种观点的人认为，鉴于a16z过去的成功和失败，他们可能掌握了一些外界不了解的内情。这种观点倾向于保持乐观，并认为不应轻易否定这种大规模投资（erulabs）。

• 还有评论指出，市场对Thinking Machines的负面情绪可能过于激烈，特别是考虑到公司拥有来自OpenAI的顶尖人才，如Murati等（pdabbadabba）。有人支持这种观点，强调Thinking Machines拥有优秀的团队，如John Schulman等，值得期待（leesec）。

• 一种批评观点认为，a16z的行为类似于软银，通过短期信号操作市场，投资可能只是泡沫的一部分（malthaus）。还有人直言，VC们可能只是希望在这场AI竞赛中获得短期收益，并不真正关心长期发展（Runsthroughit）。

补充讨论：
• 有人调侃Thinking Machines可能在进行AI领域的“军备竞赛”，暗示高额投资可能用于打击竞争对手（dandanua）。

• 一些评论表达了对Thinking Machines具体产品的困惑和好奇，指出虽然公司吸引了大量顶尖人才，但尚未公开其具体项目（beauzero）。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于，a16z对Thinking Machines的大规模投资是否基于实际潜力，还是仅仅出于炒作和市场泡沫的考虑。不同评论者对AI领域高额投资的合理性以及未来前景持不同看法。

data.title: Plasma Bigscreen rises from the dead with a better UI
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: KDE项目Plasma Bigscreen正在复活，该项目是一个用于电视的Plasma界面，最初支持已停止更新的Mycroft AI助手。由于长期贡献者Devin花费一周时间进行全面改造，Plasma Bigscreen得以重生。Devin清理了代码库，重新设计了界面，取消了面板背景，并增加了背景模糊效果。他还添加了搜索视图，使用KRunner快速查找和启动应用程序，并重做了设置应用，采用了两栏设计。显示模块和Wi-Fi、KDE Connect模块也得到了修复和更新。虽然项目尚未完成，但目标是将其重新纳入Plasma的官方发布计划，可能在6.5版本中实现。用户可以在Raspberry Pi上通过postmarketOS测试该项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux在电视或小型设备上的桌面环境和用户界面优化

不同观点：
• **bsimpson**：认为现有的桌面环境在Steam Deck等平板+手柄设备上显得不合适，建议增加类似Mobile或Bigscreen的界面选项，方便无鼠标操作。
• **whazor**：指出Linux缺乏优秀的电视界面，现有的Android TV与Steam大屏模式各有不足。希望有一个结合媒体播放与游戏功能的强大用户界面，特别是在x86架构的小型PC上。
• **giancarlostoro**：强调需要有一个硬件厂商推出预装Linux电视系统的小型设备，并建议基于Arch或Debian的发行版。同时提到目前使用Apple TV，但愿意转向Linux电视体验。
• **MattTheRealOne**：对现有的Plasma界面在mini PC上的使用体验表示认可，但指出如果应用程序没有优化，界面改进意义不大。
• **imiric**：计划在家庭影院PC上尝试新的电视界面，并希望支持外部媒体播放器如mpv，以及远程媒体库加载功能。
• **aquova**：对Plasma Bigscreen项目曾停滞表示遗憾，但对其作为Roku替代品充满期待。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现与硬件兼容性**：
  ◦ **ListeningPie** 和 **tocs3** 询问该界面是运行在外部计算机上通过HDMI连接电视，还是直接在电视硬件上运行。
  ◦ **raffael_de** 询问安装过程是否涉及写入ISO文件到USB并插入电视，或是否需要类似Amazon Fire TV stick的设备，并关心项目是否有GitHub仓库。

• **商业服务支持**：
  ◦ **IshKebab** 提到自定义电视操作系统难以支持Netflix和Prime等商业服务，并指出即使是Android也需要widevine支持，而这是商业版才有的。

• **其他工具对比**：
  ◦ **FuriouslyAdrift** 认为nVidia Shield Pro加Kodi的组合在可靠性和性能上无可替代。

• **团队与设计**：
  ◦ **andsoitis** 询问开发团队是否有设计师参与。
  ◦ **WorldPeas** 提到目前使用Linux Mint在NEC显示器上遇到的问题，并期待新界面的改进，特别是对音频问题的解决。

争议焦点：
• **最佳解决方案的选择**：不同用户对现有工具如nVidia Shield、Apple TV、Kodi等在可靠性和功能上的看法不一，反映了市场上缺乏统一的Linux电视解决方案。
• **商业服务支持的缺失**：如何在自定义Linux电视系统上支持Netflix和Prime等商业服务，尤其是在widevine支持上的困难，成为了用户关注的重要问题。

总结：用户对Linux在电视设备上的界面优化充满期待，但现有方案存在不足，尤其是在硬件兼容性、应用程序优化和商业服务支持方面。Plasma Bigscreen项目的重启带来了希望，但其实现和稳定性仍需时间验证。

44573752.article_content:
Lately, some KDE projects have seen a revival, like
Karton (the native virtual machine manager for KDE)
and the
improved ISO Image Writer.
Now, another abandoned KDE project, Plasma Bigscreen, is looking to return from the dead after long-time Plasma Mobile contributor Devin decided to spend a week overhauling the thing.
If you have not heard of it,
Plasma Bigscreen
is a Plasma shell for televisions, with original support for the now-defunct Mycroft AI assistant. It used to provide a simple launcher for apps and custom "Mycroft Skills" before development stalled, causing most distributions to drop it.
The project was left behind during the big transition to Plasma 6 last year because no one had ported it in time for the megarelease. After a friend of his started poking at the code,
Devin stepped in
to tackle the much-needed work.
He started by cleaning up the repository and then jumped into redesigning the interface, drawing inspiration from older Breeze mockups. The homescreen has been flattened, removing panel backgrounds. Here's a before-and-after comparison (click to enlarge):
One of the more visible changes is that the UI now has a background blur when you are navigating menus, giving focus to the foreground elements.
For actually finding what you want to run, you are no longer stuck scrolling through a long list, as Devin added a new search view, searching using KRunner to quickly find and launch applications.
The Settings application also got a complete redesign, adopting a simple two-pane look with a sidebar for categories. A lot of the settings modules (KCM) used hardcoded layouts, so Devin built a small component library for TV-focused UIs and ported everything over.
The rewritten Display KCM now uses the libkscreen backend, and the Wi-Fi and KDE Connect modules have been fixed and updated. Startup feedback for launching applications was also broken, and when you start up an application, a small animation now plays, similar to the one on Plasma Mobile.
For anyone who wants to test this out, you can do as Devin did by installing Plasma Bigscreen on a Raspberry Pi using postmarketOS, though you would have to compile it yourself or pull from the nightly repos to get the latest changes.
Applications like Kodi and
VacuumTube (smart TV version of YouTube)
work well with remote navigation, and some games like
SuperTuxKart
are playable.
Controller support exists, but getting TV remotes to work over HDMI CEC is still untested. The project is far from finished; it still needs an arrow-navigable virtual keyboard and a clearer long-term direction now that Mycroft is gone. Still, the goal is to get it back into the official Plasma release schedule, possibly for version 6.5.

data.title: Nearly 3 out of 4 Oracle Java users say they've been audited in the past 3 years
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 一项调查显示，73%的Oracle Java用户在过去三年中经历过审计。由于Oracle在2018年引入Java付费订阅，并在2023年改为按员工人数定价，导致许多用户面临高昂成本。近80%的用户已迁移或计划迁移到开源Java以避免高成本和审计风险。仅14%的用户打算继续使用Oracle的订阅模式。调查还发现，54%的组织每年花费超过10万美元解决许可不合规问题。IT资产管理者强调，管理现代软件许可的复杂性需要更多资源和高层支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oracle Java的商业版本使用情况及其替代方案

不同观点：
• [支持替代方案] [jsiepkes]、[hangonhn] 认为在不同的云平台（如AWS、Azure、RedHat）上使用平台自带的Java版本（如Amazon Corretto）比使用Oracle Java更合适，且可以避免Oracle的授权问题。hangonhn分享了实际经验，表示切换到AWS Corretto后，忽略Oracle的邮件并没有产生后续问题。

• [质疑Oracle Java的价值] [lijok] 提问使用Oracle Java的优势是什么，特别是相对于开源版本（OSS）的Java。

• [批评开发者依赖Oracle支持] [pvtmert] 认为Oracle之所以能收到高额费用，是因为开发者懒惰，依赖Oracle的支持团队来解决部署问题。他指出，现代JDK已经移除了很多旧的javax.*和JavaEE包，继续维护Java 1.6的基础设施是不可取的。

• [对Oracle的讽刺] [DonHopkins] 以幽默的方式表示Oracle破坏了关于Java与其他编程语言的争论，现在只需提到“lawnmower”就能结束争论。

• [对Oracle商业模式的讽刺] [msie] 以讽刺的方式表示使用Oracle的产品是为了让其创始人Larry Ellison继续富有。

• [对JVM生态的法律和实现问题的担忧] [marshray] 表示虽然JVM的生态系统强大，但其法律问题（如Google的Java相关诉讼）和依赖现有实现的难度让人失望。

补充讨论：
• [Oracle支持服务市场的需求] [ano-ther] 提到有专门为企业和政府提供Oracle支持服务的顾问市场，暗示Oracle产品的复杂性和潜在的法律风险。

争议焦点：
• Oracle Java商业版本的必要性以及其高额收费是否合理，特别是相对于开源替代方案。
• 开发者对Oracle支持的依赖是否合理，以及这种依赖是否导致不必要的成本。

44573326.article_content:
Devops
4
Nearly 3 out of 4 Oracle Java users say they've been audited in the past 3 years
4
Big Red’s changes to Java licensing also inspire exodus to open source
Lindsay Clark
Tue 15 Jul 2025
//
16:16 UTC
A survey of 500 IT asset managers in organizations that use Oracle Java has found that 73 percent have been audited in the last three years.
Deal to 'save' UK colleges £45M in Oracle Java licensing fees followed audit requests
READ MORE
At the same time, nearly eight out of 10 Oracle Java users said they had migrated, or planned to shift, to open source Java to try to avoid the risk and high costs of the dominant vendor's development and runtime environments.
Oracle introduced a paid subscription for Java in September 2018, and in January 2023, it
decided to switch its pricing model
to per employee rather than per user, creating a steep price hike for many users. In July 2023, Gartner recorded users experiencing
price increases of between two and five times
when they switched to the new licensing model.
Two years later, the survey conducted by market research firm Dimensional Research showed only 14 percent of Oracle Java users intended to stick with the vendor's subscription model.
The
research
was commissioned and authored by ITAM Forum, an independent group representing IT asset managers and Azul, which provides open source Java products and services.
It points out that Oracle introduced four licensing and pricing policy changes between 2020 and 2023. "To avoid Oracle's price hikes, Java customers must upgrade to the latest Java version every three years to continue receiving free support under the Oracle Java SE Universal Subscription or otherwise migrate to an open-source alternative," the report said.
'We had to educate Oracle about our contract,' CIO says after Big Red audit
Oracle cuts support for South African energy biz Eskom in long-running licensing dispute
Only 1 in 10 Oracle Java users want to stay with Big Red
Oracle's Java price hikes push CIOs to brew new licensing strategies
The survey also revealed the cost of audits. While vendors have the right to charge for copyright-protected software, 25 percent of survey participants said complex software configurations make tracking application usage more difficult. At the same time, 29 percent of ITAM professionals reported that their organizations struggle to manage this information, especially when tracking software usage across teams or between on-premises and cloud platforms. More than half of survey participants (54 percent) said their organization spent more than $100,000 a year on resolving licensing non-compliance issues, while 27 percent said the figure was more than $500,000 a year.
"The results highlight a fundamental mismatch between the complexity of modern software licensing and the resources organizations rely on to effectively manage software compliance," said Martin Thompson, founder of the ITAM Forum.
He added that ITAM professionals need the resources and executive buy-in to ensure compliance and successful license management.
Oracle has been offered the opportunity to respond to the survey. ®

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对分形（特别是Mandelbrot及相关变体）的讨论，包括技术实现、个人经验和算法优化等方面。

不同观点：
• **对分形算法的技术探讨**：
  - [mg] 提到并非所有分形都能通过迭代公式 f(z,c) 表达，并分享了自己通过不同方法发现的分形例子，即基于高斯整数除法的可视化分形。
  - [ttoinou] 分享了自己发现的分形变体 "Monkelbrot" 的公式，强调其在保持与原始Mandelbrot相似性的同时，具备不同的数学特性。

• **个人经验和历史回顾**：
  - [mreid] 感叹现代浏览器中通过解释性语言快速渲染分形的技术进步，回忆自己小时候用68000汇编语言编写分形渲染程序的经历。

data.title: Hierarchical Modeling (H-Nets)
data.author: marviel
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种新的AI架构——层次网络（H-Nets），它通过动态分块机制从原始数据中学习和压缩有意义的概念，解决了当前AI模型对高分辨率原始数据处理能力有限的问题。H-Nets由编码网络、主网络和解码网络组成，能够更好地随数据规模扩展，尤其在中文、代码和DNA等无明显分词边界的领域表现突出。H-Nets还能通过更深层次的结构提升性能，并增强对输入数据小扰动的鲁棒性。该架构有助于多模态数据融合和长时段推理，同时提高训练和推理效率，为下一代AI模型的发展提供了新方向。研究全文和模型权重已在arXiv和HuggingFace发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：H-Net语言模型的优势及潜在应用

不同观点：
• **marviel**：H-Net展示了三个重要成果：1. H-Net在数据扩展性上优于使用BPE标记化的最先进Transformer，可以直接从原始字节学习，尤其在中文、代码和DNA等没有自然分词边界的领域表现更突出。2. H-Net可以通过堆叠学习更深层次的结构，进一步提高性能。3. H-Net对输入数据的小扰动（如大小写）更加鲁棒，为创建更符合人类推理的模型提供了途径。

• **modeless**：支持H-Net的方向，认为需要更多层次的结构以高效地泛化到更长序列并具有更高层次的结构。提到Byte Latent Transformers的扩展想法与H-Net类似，并分享了另一篇关于H-Net的文章链接。

• **macawfish**：提出可以考虑更广泛的图表示以及层次化缩减，不完全认同“语言本质上是层次化的”观点，认为不必局限于单一层次结构，可以学习多个层次并学会如何在它们之间调制。

• **cs702**：初步阅读论文后认为其有趣且可信，提到H-Net的层次组合和路由方面让他想起其他类似的工作，如heinsen_routing，但承认两者有不同之处。

• **notreallymetho**：提到H-Net让他联想到自己曾做过的相关工作，并分享了相关论文链接。

• **vannevar**：质疑H-Net是否真的与现有的AI架构不同，认为H-Net本质上仍然是通过推理输入的层次结构来预处理输入，而所有模型在训练时基本都这样做。

• **aeon_ai**：认为H-Net可能对记忆形成、巩固和管理有重要意义。

• **gdiamos**：关心H-Net如何处理图像。

• **cubefox**：疑问H-Net是否会取代Transformer，尤其是在Mamba未能成功的情况下。

补充讨论：
• 关于H-Net是否真正不同于现有AI架构的争议（**vannevar**）。
• H-Net在不同数据类型（如代码、DNA）上的扩展性和表现（**marviel**）。
• H-Net在图像处理方面的潜在应用（**gdiamos**）。
• H-Net是否可能取代Transformer的讨论（**cubefox**）。
• 对H-Net层次结构单一性的质疑与扩展思考（**macawfish**）。

44574990.article_content:
Jul 11, 2025
Â·
Research
Hierarchical modeling
Hierarchical modeling
Albert Gu
Brandon Wang
The best AI architectures in use today treat all inputs equally. They process each input with the same amount of compute, without explicitly grouping related inputs into higher level concepts. While these architectures have achieved impressive results across domains, this lack of hierarchy has some fundamental limitations.
Models have difficulty learning from high resolution, raw data, requiring inputs to be pre-processed into meaningful tokens for strong performance.
The use of hand-crafted pre-processing steps (e.g. tokenization) can cause models to fail unexpectedly with small perturbations in the input data.
Models waste compute on tokens that are easy to predict and not informative.
More importantly, information is fundamentally hierarchical. In language, ideas are chunked in characters, words, sentences, and paragraphs; in images, pixels are chunked in edges, shapes, and objects; in audio, raw waveforms are grouped into phonemes, sentences, and conversation turns. As humans, we consume raw information and group it in meaningful ways that allow us to reason and make connections at different levels of abstraction, from low level units to the high level ideas. This is core to intelligence. We believe hierarchical models will address several of the fundamental limitations and shortcomings of todayâs architectures.
Weâre excited to announce our latest research collaboration on
hierarchical networks (H-Nets)
, a new architecture that natively models hierarchy from raw data. The core of the H-Net architecture is a dynamic chunking mechanism that learns to segment and compress raw data into meaningful concepts for modeling. It has three components: an encoder network, the main network, and a decoder network. The core of the encoder network is a routing module, which uses a similarity score to predict groups of meaningful chunks that should be grouped together and compressed for the main network. The main network can be any sequence to sequence model, and is responsible for next token prediction over these higher level chunks. Finally, the decoder network learns to decode chunks back into raw data, with a smoothing module for stabilizing learning.
H-Net demonstrates three important results on language modeling:
H-Nets scale better with data than state-of-the-art Transformers with BPE tokenization, while learning directly from raw bytes. This improved scaling is even more pronounced on domains without natural tokenization boundaries, like Chinese, code, and DNA.
H-Nets can be stacked together to learn from deeper hierarchies, which further improves performance.
H-Nets are significantly more robust to small perturbations in input data like casing, showing an avenue for creating models that are more robust and aligned with human reasoning.
Our investment in this research is part of our larger push to build the next-generation of AI models that are multimodal, highly efficient, and reason and improve over long horizons. State space models represented our first research advancement, enabling stateful models that can compress information over long contexts. We believe H-Nets, and hierarchical modeling, are the key next step to addressing fundamental challenges in AI:
Multimodal understanding and generation:
A key challenge in multimodal modeling is fusing multiple streams of data. This is a difficult today, since different modalities are tokenized at different rates. For example, language is tokenized into subwords, while audio is tokenized as raw waveforms or downsampled codecs. This makes them difficult to model jointly. Hierarchical models like H-Net provide a promising path to fuse these multimodal streams at a higher abstraction level, enabling better transfer, reasoning, and understanding across modalities.
Long-context reasoning:
H-Nets unlock long context reasoning by chunking information into semantically meaningful units at higher levels of abstraction. This compression makes it easier for models to understand and reason across large inputs, particularly with deeper and deeper hierarchies. Hierarchical architectures will enable models that understand their environment from raw data and reason at appropriate levels of abstraction over long horizons.
Efficient training and inference:
Todayâs architectures use the same amount of compute for every token, even though some tokens are less informative and easier to predict than others. Inference time optimizations, like speculative decoding, exploit this property to speed up computation on easier to predict tokens. With H-Nets, this is built directly into the architecture, by handling tokens that are easier to predict with lightweight encoder and decoder modules.
For more, read our full preprint on
arXiv
. Weâve also released checkpoints for H-Net 2-stage XL, H-Net 1-stage XL, and H-Net 1-stage L on
HuggingFace
.

data.title: Lorem Gibson
data.author: DyslexicAtheist
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为Lorem Gibson的网站，该网站生成基于威廉·吉布森作品的填充文本。用户可以刷新页面以获取更多文字内容。文章还提到对改进建议可发送至@davidtweaver，并欢迎捐款支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对"Lorem Gibson"风格文本生成器的评价与建议，以及对类似文本生成工具的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持并赞赏**：
   - [allenu]: 总体喜欢这个想法，但希望句子首字母大写和破折号问题能修正，如去除破折号间的空格。
   - [nodefortytwo]: 非常喜欢这个想法，并分享了使用Grok工具生成的类似风格文本，展示了对该风格的认可。
   - [Brajeshwar]: 回忆了过去类似的Lorem Ipsum变体，表示这种复古风格很有趣，并提到自己仍在使用类似的键盘快捷方式。

• **提出改进建议**：
   - [mNovak]: 虽然觉得创意有趣，但期望生成更符合语法规则的句子，并认为实现正确的大小写并不难。
   - [rcarmo]: 认为缺少一些标志性的元素（如"the sky was the color of television tuned to a dead channel"），但对整体表示认可。
   - [dzdt]: 提到现代LLM（大型语言模型）技术可以实现更好的结果，建议使用nanoGPT训练Gibson风格的语料库。

• **其他创意或幽默回应**：
   - [jl6]: 用一种戏谑的方式模仿生成文本的风格，展示了对该生成器输出的理解和幽默感。
   - [hungryhobbit]: 提到Lorem Gibson在其他地方的引用，并询问发帖者是否参考了某篇文章，显示了对背景内容的关注。
   - [tshaddox]: 开玩笑地建议使用Henrik Ibsen的风格，提供了一种不同的文本生成思路。
   - [wheybags]、[ilikecakeandpie]、[f4c39012]、[dfxm12]: 以幽默或创意方式回应，包括模仿Lorem Ipsum的语法或引用流行文化元素，显示了对该话题的轻松态度。

• **反思与质疑**：
   - [paulryanrogers]: 提出对这类工具的反思，质疑作者对这种文本生成方式的看法。
   - [efitz]: 关注生成文本中的语法问题，特别指出缺少动词。

补充讨论：
- 评论中提到了多种与Lorem Ipsum类似的文本生成工具和风格，如DeLorean Ipsum和过去的各种Lorem变体，显示出对多样化占位文本的需求和兴趣。
- 一些评论者关注文本的语法和格式问题，表明在创意文本生成中，语法正确性和格式标准化仍然是值得注意的方面。
- 争议的焦点主要在于生成文本的语法正确性和风格还原度，部分评论者认为可以借助现代技术实现更高质量的输出。

data.author: Petiver
data.article_summary: 文章《Human Stigmergy: The world is my task list》由Marco Giancotti撰写，探讨了通过观察昆虫的“刺激性反应”（stigmergy）现象，人类如何利用环境作为外部记忆工具。蚂蚁和白蚁没有中央计划，通过信息素标记环境来协作建造复杂的结构。作者受到启发，认为人类也可以通过将任务外化到环境中来克服记忆力差的缺点。例如，把打气筒放在出门必经之路上以提醒自己给自行车打气。这种方法利用物理环境作为记忆载体，避免了依赖大脑或数字设备，展示了分散式记忆和行动的有效性。文章强调了记忆不仅限于大脑，还可以通过物理方式实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：记忆与组织方式的有效性，以及技术对记忆和任务管理的影响

不同观点：
• pimlottc认为，随着事物数字化，过去依赖物理文件位置来追踪任务状态的 decentralized 系统逐渐消失。他通过在政府 legacy 系统中的经验，指出物理文件位置如何自然地反映任务状态，每个阶段都知道文件的去向。
• munificent强调通过逻辑归类来减少对记忆的依赖，采用自我对话的方式记住物品位置，但由于家庭成员的ADHD导致物品随机放置，使得这种方法受限。
• canistel分享自己无法多任务处理，学习 JavaScript 式的单线程任务管理方法，将新任务放在列表底部，紧急任务放在顶部。
• keeda提到 stigmergy（群体智慧）在 decentralized 系统中的潜力，尽管基于该原理的 Ant Colony Optimization 未能实现预期效果，但在 decentralized 系统中仍有价值。
• davidjhall描述 SDAM（自传体记忆严重缺陷）的影响，指出这种记忆缺陷带来的持续困惑感。
• entropie认为物理记忆方法（如在门口放垃圾袋）仍需一定的记忆参与，且需要通过反复训练来建立 IF -> THEN 触发机制。
• felipemesquita分享将车钥匙放在需要带走的物品下以避免忘记，尽管有时需要花费时间寻找。
• bobson381提出“物理记忆”概念，认为现实世界本身就是一种高级计算环境，数字地图只是辅助。
• FredPret将经济视为一种 decentralized 协调机制，通过价格信号实现大规模协调。
• lucaspauker认为大型语言模型（LLMs）充当了人类的集体记忆，通过与它们互动，可以减少个人记忆的需求。
• OgsyedIE通过 transhumanist 视角，探讨外接大脑（exocortices）在当前技术下的局限性，尤其是对默认模式下的记忆生成和梦境的影响。
• readthenotes1分享个人经历，因将车钥匙放在购物袋并放入冰箱导致寻找困难，强调通过固定习惯避免记忆失误。

补充讨论：
1. 争议焦点在于物理记忆方法是否完全摆脱对大脑记忆的依赖。entropie和munificent认为仍需一定记忆参与，而felipemesquita和readthenotes1的经历显示习惯和固定放置能有效减少记忆负担。
2. 讨论中涉及技术对记忆的影响，如LLMs和exocortices，探讨如何通过技术增强或替代人类记忆功能。
3. decentralized 系统与 centralized 数据库的对比，pimlottc和keeda强调 decentralized 系统的自然优势，而现实中技术发展往往趋向 centralized 解决方案。

44574905.article_content:
Human Stigmergy
The world is my task list
Marco Giancotti
,
July	10, 2025
Marco Giancotti
,
July	10, 2025
Cover image:
Termite mound cross-section, Wikimedia Commons
Termites and ants have no central planning. There are no
architect ants
in a nest-building project, no sponsors or supervisors, no instructions. Each worker is unaware and completely uninterested in what form the final mega-structure will take. No blueprints are to be found in any of their minds or outside them. Yet they build them all the time, and very well, too.
Their substitute for plans and blueprints is what biologists call
stigmergy
. Each worker instinctively marks the environment with pheromones as it works—the termite infuses it in the dollops of mud it deposits, the ant marks the path it took to find food—then other workers smell the pheromone and act based on it. This is repeated by each insect, and it is all they need to build and stock their great cathedrals, complete with effective ventilation shafts, highways leading straight to the best sources of food, and everything else they need to thrive.
This topic never ceases to fascinate me. It's a demonstration that great things can be achieved together in a fully decentralized way. Intelligence can be distributed rather than fenced off. The exercise of power isn't the only way.
But stigmergy interests me in yet another way—a more mundane and pragmatic way: it is proof that there are other kinds of memory besides the "mental".
I have a
terrible memory
, and I forget the concrete and ephemeral duties and to-dos of my daily life all the time. I've learned to trust my ability to remember to do things exactly 0%. I live on the solid certainty that I will forget things. To-do apps and notes help, but they're never enough. Digital supports have the fatal flaw of requiring me to remember to check my digital devices—something I do often, but not necessarily when I need it.
A single termite isn't very smart. I doubt it even knows what it is doing while carrying its ball-shaped bricks up its half-constructed mound. I'm grateful to it for just how low it sets the bar for me. Can memory-less Marco learn something from that termite? I can't secrete pungent pheromones (not intentionally, at least), and that's probably a good thing. But I have two very useful appendages with many accurate fingers working for me, and those should function as good substitutes.
Eusocial insects shape the environment around them as a form of external, localized memory. I do the same! If I decide I want to refill my bicycle's tires with air the next time I go out, I don't even try to commit that to memory, nor do I write a memo on Google Keep: I immediately take the floor pump and place it on the path out of my room. When I need to remember to throw trash away, my wife or I put the bags right at the foot of the front door. To keep track of how many hours I've worked in a day, I move Lego bricks from one side of my computer's monitor to the other at every periodic break.
All these acts remove the need for me to remember, even to know. I could hit my head and have my short-term memory wiped clean, and simply looking at the pump, the garbage bag, the toy brick would instantly inform me of what I'm supposed to do.
It's not just me. People seem to do this all the time without much thought: they leave their umbrellas in the foyer right next to their shoes, to remember to check the weather; they drape their jackets over the backs of their seats in cafes, both to find the seats again and to signal to others to look elsewhere; they tie knots in strings to keep track of their lives.
This is fabulous. We tend to think of memory and mind-related concepts as purely abstract, separate, and invisible processes that happen somewhere up there—at best in the brain, at worst in a separate "world of the mind"
à la
Descartes, entirely disconnected from the "physical world".
Humble ants teach us otherwise. ●

Termite mound cross-section, Wikimedia Commons

data.title: Hazel: A live functional programming environment with typed holes
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: Hazel是一个基于类型理论的实时函数式编程环境，支持带类型的占位符。它可以在线体验，当前主要开发分支为`dev`。要构建和运行Hazel，需安装OCaml 5.2.0、opam 2.0及以上版本和npm，然后通过一系列命令克隆、安装依赖和启动开发服务器。Hazel使用ReasonML编写，提供了与OCaml相互转换的工具。对于使用VS Code的开发者，建议安装一些扩展以支持ReasonML开发，如ocaml-platform和Bracket Pair Colorizer 2。对于NeoVim用户，推荐设置LSP以获得更好的编程体验。详细信息和安装步骤可参考相关文档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hazel编程环境的介绍与功能，特别是其“类型孔洞”（typed holes）特性，以及用户对该工具的反馈和联想。

不同观点：
• [dang]: 提到Hazel的相关链接，并询问是否有其他相关的讨论，显示出对更多信息的兴趣。
• [bitbasher]: 指出"Hazel"这个名字与其他项目（如Cherno的游戏引擎）重名，可能引起混淆。
• [Awtem]: 表示对Hazel的喜爱，但希望在主页和GitHub的README中看到更多示例和截图，以获得更直观的理解。
• [burnt-resistor]: 以幽默的方式建议将项目命名为"Donut"，这是一种轻松的命名建议，没有实质性讨论功能。
• [dub_gui]: 对Hazel的实时演示表示赞赏，并提供了一个实时演示链接，显示出对实际演示的积极反馈。
• [Asraelite]: 通过对比Rust中的`!`和TypeScript中的`never`，询问类型孔洞在类型系统中的独特之处，显示出对技术细节的关注。
• [andsoitis]: 以幽默的方式解释“类型孔洞驱动开发”，通过文字游戏强调了类型和孔洞的关系。
• [eterps]: 提出将LLM（大型语言模型）代码生成与Hazel结合的想法，显示出对未来技术整合的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 用户对Hazel的实时演示和类型孔洞特性表现出较大兴趣，但也有用户希望看到更多示例和截图以便更好地理解。
• 对“类型孔洞”的技术细节存在一定的好奇和疑问，特别是与其他编程语言特性的对比。
• 用户对项目名称可能引起的混淆表示关注，并提出了轻松的命名建议。
• 有用户开始思考Hazel与LLM等新兴技术的结合，显示出对未来发展的期待。

Hazel
Hazel is a live functional-programming environment rooted in the principles of
type theory. You can find the relevant papers and more motivation at
the Hazel
website
.
You can try Hazel online: the
dev
branch is the main branch at the
moment. Every other branch that has been pushed to GitHub and successfully builds
can also be accessed at:
https://hazel.org/build/<branch_name>
Building and Running Hazel
Short version
If you already have
ocaml
version 5.2.0, at least version 2.0 of
opam
, and
npm
installed, you can build Hazel by running the following commands.
git clone git@github.com:hazelgrove/hazel.git
cd hazel
make deps
make dev
To view Hazel, you have to serve it, on localhost for development (you can't
run it from a
file:///
URL due to browser restrictions on e.g. web workers.)
If you have
python3
on your path, you can use the Python server via
make serve
, then navigate to
http://0.0.0.0:8000/
in your browser.
Alternatively, if you would live hot reloading, you can use
make hot
instead of
make serve
.
Otherwise, run
make echo-html-dir
which will echo the directory that needs
to be served using some other server of your choice.
Long Version
If you are unfamiliar with
ocaml
or
opam
, do not have them installed, or
just get stuck, we recommend you follow the step-by-step installation
instructions contained in
INSTALL.md
.
Contributing
From OCaml to ReasonML
Hazel is written in ReasonML, which is a syntactic sugar atop OCaml.
This link lets you type OCaml and see what the corresponding ReasonML syntax is:
https://reasonml.github.io/en/try
.
This is useful if you are trying to figure out the ReasonML syntax for something
that you know the OCaml syntax for.
You can also convert between OCaml and ReasonML syntax at the terminal using
refmt
at the terminal. See
refmt --help
for the details.
Suggested Extensions for VS Code
Most of our team uses Visual Studio Code (VS Code) to write code.
If you use VS Code, here are a few extensions that might be helpful.
This extension provides full support for editing ReasonML source code and
relevant tools:
ocaml-platform
Due to Reason's poor parse errors, unbalanced parentheses can be difficult
to find.  The following extensions help with that.
Bracket Pair Colorizer 2
Indenticator
indent-rainbow
In addition to these extensions, enabling the breadcrumbs bar can make
navigating a large code base easier. There are multiple ways to make the
breadcrumbs bar visible:
Click
View
/
Show Breadcrumbs
from the menu bar.
Press
Ctrl+Shift+P
(macOS:
Cmd+Shift+P
), start typing
breadcrumbs
, and
select
View: Toggle Breadcrumbs
from the dropdown menu to toggle breadcrumbs
on and off.
Press
Ctrl+Shift+.
to start breadcrumbs navigation.
Suggested Setup for NeoVim
If you enjoy your Vim binding and Vim setup, the following may help you set up your Reason IDE in NeoVim.
If you use vim, I recommend you to switch to NeoVim since it has a better support for multi-thread,
and thus less likely to block you when you are programming.
To set up the LSP (Language Server Protocol), you need to set up your Language Client for Neovim and Language Server for ocaml.
ocaml-language-server
LanguageClient-neovim
After installing the previous two, you may want to copy the following to your neovim config file.
(assuming
npm
have ocaml-language-server installed under
/usr/bin
)
let g:LanguageClient_serverCommands = {
\ 'ocaml': ['/usr/bin/ocaml-language-server', '--stdio'],
\ 'reason': ['/usr/bin/ocaml-language-server', '--stdio']
\ }
" LanguageClient-neovim
nnoremap <F5> :call LanguageClient_contextMenu()<CR>
" Or map each action separately
nnoremap <silent> K :call LanguageClient#textDocument_hover()<CR>
nnoremap <silent> gd :call LanguageClient#textDocument_definition()<CR>
nnoremap <silent> gr :call LanguageClient#textDocument_references()<CR>
nnoremap <silent> gf :call Langu

data.title: The Story of Mel, A Real Programmer, Annotated (1996)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 《The Story of Mel, A Real Programmer》是由Ed Nather撰写的经典故事，描述了一位名叫Mel的真正程序员，他通过巧妙的手工优化，在早期计算机上实现了高效的程序运行。Mel以其出色的编程技巧和对机器底层的深刻理解而闻名。Erik Brunvand为此故事做了注释，解释了其中的技术细节和历史背景，帮助现代读者理解早期计算机编程的挑战和魅力。这篇文章通过生动的叙述展现了早期计算机时代的编程文化和程序员的智慧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“LGP-30计算机”及其相关历史、技术细节、人物“Mel”的讨论

不同观点：
• **drfuchs** 提到LGP-30的详细手册可以在网上找到，并分享了自己在1973年学习LGP-30汇编语言的经历。他认为从底层机器语言学起有助于理解计算机的运行原理，但这种方法在今天不再普遍。
• **alnwlsn** 提到YouTuber David收到了LGP-21计算机以及一些LGP-30代码，其中包括Mel编写的程序。尽管Mel的代码比传闻中更清晰，但LGP-30的自修改代码是一个预期功能。他还提到目前没有找到太多关于LGP-21的文档，研究这些代码可能有助于理解LGP-21。
• **anyfoo** 提到一个关于Mel的播客，并建议在听之前先了解“The Story of Mel”这篇文章，以更好地理解播客内容。
• **naniwaduni** 分享了一个小知识点：LGP-30的十六进制数字使用的是非标准的“0-9fgjkqw”表示法。

补充讨论：
• **dang** 提到关于Mel的讨论在社区中时有出现，并列举了过去几年相关讨论的链接，显示出社区对Mel及LGP-30相关历史的持续兴趣。
• **ksenzee** 幽默地指出，1996年的注释中对“硬盘”和“软盘”的解释现在可能需要进一步注释。
• **oc1** 提到遇到过像Mel一样的程序员，他们拒绝适应新技术和AI工具，但自己却在快速发展并部署应用。
• **habedi0** 简单地问道“The Story of Mel”是否足够说明问题。
• **anteloper** 和 **reverendsteveii** 都表达了对“The Story of Mel”这篇文章的喜爱，前者称其为精彩的阅读，后者将其比作互联网时代的“申命记”。
• **BruceEel** 对LGP-30的“磁鼓记忆”是否存在照片表示好奇。
• **andybak** 幽默地评论说“要是有超链接就好了”，暗示早期文档缺乏现代的链接便利。

争议焦点：
• 关于从底层机器语言学起是否仍然是必要的教育方法存在不同看法。drfuchs认为这种方法对他有效，但现代不一定普遍适用。

总体来看，讨论围绕LGP-30和Mel的历史、技术细节、代码研究及其在计算机历史中的地位展开，参与者分享了个人经历、资源链接和对相关技术的兴趣。

data.title: Mostly dead influential programming languages (2020)
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了历史上具有重要影响的一些编程语言，尤其是那些被认为“ mostly dead”（大多已消亡）的语言。作者批评了一个将Go列为“最具影响力”却忽略ALGOL、Smalltalk和ML等语言的榜单，认为其违背了“历史影响力”的初衷。文章强调了许多老旧语言的重要性，如COBOL和ALGOL，并解释了它们对现代编程的影响。

文章首先介绍了如何判断编程语言的影响力，强调引用是关键证据，并提出了通过语法相似性等启发式方法来追溯影响。随后详细讨论了COBOL和ALGOL两种语言的历史背景、重要性和消亡原因。COBOL引入了记录数据的概念，对现代数据结构有重要影响，但因复杂性和学术界的忽视逐渐被取代。ALGOL虽几乎消亡，但其对词法作用域、结构化编程等诸多现代编程概念的贡献不可忽视。

文章最后指出，历史是复杂的，编程语言的影响往往跨越多个世代，需要深入挖掘和理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对几种历史编程语言的现状和影响的评价

不同观点：
• **COBOL的贡献与影响**：
  - **vincent-manis** 认为COBOL在程序和数据跨机器可移植性方面的创新具有革命性意义，尽管现在被视为理所当然。COBOL的设计大大减少了移植问题，这种影响在现代编程中仍然存在。
  - **Rochus** 则直接反驳COBOL"已死"的说法，指出COBOL仍然处理全球超过70%的商业交易，认为其在现代系统中依然具有重要地位。

• **ALGOL及其变种的影响**：
  - **jamesfinlayson** 认为ALGOL是四种母语言中最"死"的一种，尽管其他语言如COBOL、LISP和FORTRAN仍然有大量遗留系统或应用。
  - **Taniwha** 则为Algol-68辩护，认为它引入了许多对后来语言有重大影响的特性，如'struct'、'union'等，只是由于其严格的数学定义和复杂性导致其不受欢迎。

• **函数式编程语言的演化**：
  - **jasperry** 不同意文章中关于Haskell的兴起导致SML消亡的观点，认为SML和OCaml仍在发展，且这两个分支的函数式编程语言一直在共同演化。

• **Ada的现状**：
  - **geophile** 提到Ada虽然有特定领域的应用，但并未像C语言那样广泛流行，并提出对Ada为何未能在竞争中取胜的疑问。

• **其他语言的讨论**：
  - **somat** 指出SQL的语法与COBOL有相似之处，尤其是在尝试模仿自然语言方面。
  - **askvictor** 质疑文章中关于Python不是"真正的"面向对象语言的说法，认为Python符合一切皆对象的定义。
  - **ck45** 提到Modula-3虽然基本消亡，但对其他语言如Go有影响。
  - **zzo38computer** 和 **geophile** 回忆了使用BASIC、Pascal、APL、COBOL、PL/1等语言的经历，并讨论了PL/1中的一些独特功能。

• **APL到MATLAB的演化**：
  - **DrNosferatu** 指出MATLAB是APL的ASCII后代，认为文章中未充分说明这一点，并提到从APL到MATLAB/R再到NumPy的发展路径。

• **Pascal的衰落**：
  - **mikewarot** 将Pascal的衰落归咎于Borland的管理决策，认为他们没有坚持发展Pascal，而是转向了C++和"企业级"解决方案，最终导致C#的兴起和Pascal的没落。

• **Perl的现状**：
  - **ab_testing** 提到Perl正在逐渐衰落，新包越来越少，CPAN上许多包未维护，表明Perl正在缓慢消亡。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及多种历史编程语言的现状、演化及影响，讨论了这些语言是否"已死"或仍在使用，并提供了许多个人经验和观察。
- 争议的焦点主要集中在COBOL和ALGOL的现状以及SML和Haskell在函数式编程中的关系。

44545050.article_content:
The other day I read
20 most significant programming languages in history
, a “preposterous table I just made up.” He certainly got preposterous right: he lists Go as “most significant” but not ALGOL, Smalltalk, or ML. He also leaves off Pascal because it’s “mostly dead”. Preposterous! That defeats the whole point of what “significant in history” means.
So let’s talk about some “mostly dead” languages and why they matter so much.
Disclaimer:
Yeah not all of these are dead and not all of these are forgotten. Like most people have heard of Smalltalk, right? Also there’s probably like a billion mistakes in this, because when you’re doing a survey of 60 years of computing history you’re gonna get some things wrong. Feel free to yell at me if you see anything!
Disclaimer 2:
Yeah I know some of these are “first to invent” and others are “first to popularize”. History is complicated!
Detecting Influence
Before we start, a quick primer on finding influence. Just knowing that X was the first language with feature Z doesn’t mean that X actually
influenced
Z. While
Absys
was arguably the first logic programming language, almost all of logic programming actually stems from Prolog, which was developed independently. Ultimately there’s only one way to know for certain that X influenced Y: citation. This means one of
Y cites X in its reference manual
Y cites a paper that cites X
The author of Y says “we were influenced by X.”
Citations are transitive. Sometimes the language manual for Q lists motivating document R, which cites paper S as an inspiration, which mentions it got the ideas from language T. Then we know that T influenced Q, even if the chain is several steps long. This means digging through many sources to find a signal. To speed this up we use heuristics to decide where to look.
One effective heuristic is programming language
cognates
. It’s very rare for languages to independently come up with the same syntax. So if two languages share some syntax, one likely influenced the other. For example: even without reading design decisions by Matz, we know that Ruby was influenced by Smalltalk, as they both filter a list with a
select
method. This isn’t conclusive evidence. Maybe Matz came up with it independently, or maybe Ruby and Smalltalk were both influenced by a common ancestor. But it gives us a place to start looking.
The Languages
COBOL
Background:
CODASYL, 1960. COBOL is shaped by the business/science split in computing. At that time high-level industry languages were either used for engineering computations or managing data. The engineers had all gotten behind FORTRAN while the business world was a mess of COMTRAN, FLOW-MATIC, and others, so the Department of Defense got a committee together to make a single universal business language. That’s COBOL.
COBOL was one of the four “mother” languages, along with ALGOL, FORTRAN, and LISP. While we consider it a punchline today, it was once the most popular language in the world. It still runs a lot of our legacy business systems.
Significance
: In terms of syntax and semantics we don’t see much of COBOL in modern computing. COBOL’s most important addition is the concept of record data. In FORTRAN and ALGOL, your only data structure was the static array. In COBOL, though, you could read in structured files with hierarchical data, and it would automatically destructure them into the representative variables. This was a precursor to modern day structs.
Cause of Death
: Two factors here. One: COBOL had no overlap with other PLT efforts. Very few people built on COBOL. This meant that second or third generation languages, which built on the lessons of their ancestors, had almost no COBOL DNA. This was less intrinsic problem of COBOL and more because of the academia’s disdain for its creation process. CODASYL was a business group and obviously wasn’t worth paying attention to.
1
COBOL was also enormously complex, even for today’s languages. This means that COBOL compilers lagged contemporaries on microcomputers and minicomputers, giving spaces for other languages to flourish and eventually outcompete it.
ALGOL
Background
: The ALGOL committee, 1960. ALGOL-58 came out two years before but was quickly superseded, so I’m wrapping them into each other. The committee wanted to make a good language for researching algorithms. In other words, ALGOL was a formalized “pseudocode”.
Of the four mother languages, ALGOL is the most “dead”; Everybody still knows about LISP,
2
COBOL still powers tons of legacy systems, and most scientific packages still have some FORTRAN. But I’ve met plenty of programmers who haven’t even heard of ALGOL. You’d think it’d be the least important of the mother languages, but it’s the opposite. Of the four, only LISP comes anywhere
close
to the pervasive importance of ALGOL.
Significance
: Let’s see: lexical scoping, structured programming, nested functions, formal language specifications, call-by-name semantics, BNF grammars, block comments… every moder

data.title: Study finds AI tools made open source software developers 19 percent slower
data.author: samizdis
data.article_summary: 一项由METR进行的随机对照试验发现，有经验的开放源代码开发者在使用当前AI工具辅助编码任务时，效率反而降低了19%。尽管开发者预期AI工具能节省24%的时间，且认为实际节省了20%的时间，但结果显示AI工具增加了审查输出、提示系统和等待生成结果的时间，导致总体效率下降。研究还指出，AI工具在处理复杂、高标准的真实代码库时表现不佳，尤其当需要 tacit knowledge 或隐性要求时。然而，研究人员仍对未来AI工具在简单项目或改进后的潜力持乐观态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在开发者工作流中的有效性和影响

不同观点：
• [支持AI工具提升生产力]  
一些开发者（如sarlalian）认为，尽管初期学习曲线陡峭且令人沮丧，但一旦掌握AI工具并调整工作流，开发效率可以显著提高。sarlalian个人感觉在适应工具后，自己的生产力提高了约2倍。他强调，尽管初期使用像ChatGPT这样的工具时效果不佳，但随着使用经验的积累和工具的优化，体验大幅改善。

• [AI工具可能降低效率]  
i_niks_86和hoppp则认为，AI工具在处理复杂任务时可能反而拖慢开发速度。他们指出，如果开发者在不完全理解内部机制的情况下依赖AI工具，会导致大量时间浪费在调试、反向工程和调整生成代码上。尤其是开源项目中，代码的可维护性和正确性更为重要，过度依赖AI工具可能导致效率下降。hoppp进一步分享了自己的负面体验，认为对于复杂功能，调试生成代码的时间可能比手写代码更长。

• [AI工具减轻开发疲劳]  
pitched提出了一种不同的观点，认为使用AI工具尽管可能在某些情况下降低效率，但它减少了开发者的疲劳感。他表示，经过较长时间的AI工具使用后，自己感觉比传统开发方式下更轻松，因此从长远来看，AI工具在精神上的负担较小，具有一定价值。

补充讨论：
• 学习曲线与经验积累：sarlalian和hoppp都提到了AI工具的高学习曲线，但前者认为通过不断学习和调整可以克服这一障碍，而后者认为即便熟练掌握，复杂任务的处理仍然耗时。

• AI工具的适用场景：i_niks_86强调AI工具在需要高度人类判断的场景中表现不佳，而hoppp则具体指出，AI工具在生成简单UI组件时表现较好，但在复杂功能生成上效果不佳。

争议焦点：  
AI工具在开发工作流中的实际效果存在分歧。部分开发者认为其能提升生产力，而另一些开发者则认为其在复杂任务上可能拖慢速度并增加调试负担。此外，AI工具是否能减轻开发者的疲劳感也是一个讨论点，但未有定论。
