data.title: I'm Switching to Python and Actually Liking It
data.author: cesarsotovalero
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了其在使用Python进行编程，特别是开发AI应用过程中的经验和心得。作者提到，由于AI领域的蓬勃发展，Python作为该领域的主流编程语言，吸引了其关注。尽管作者之前曾使用Python编写小脚本，但直到开始构建实际的AI应用时，才真正认真对待Python。文章介绍了Python的优势，如丰富的库生态、更快的编译器（如Cython）、以及语法改进。同时，作者强调了从Jupyter notebook或简单脚本转向生产级应用开发的挑战，并分享了其项目结构和常用工具，包括使用单仓库（monorepo）管理前后端代码、VSCode配置、GitHub Actions自动化工作流等。作者还讨论了项目目录结构，并提供了一些配置示例。最后，作者邀请读者分享其他有用的工具和建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python语言的优缺点、历史发展、在不同领域的应用及其工具链（如包管理和虚拟环境）的讨论。

不同观点：
• [reedf1] 认为Python通过像@dataclass这样的语法糖隐藏了其早期的一些“丑陋”部分（如__init__、__new__），但这些“丑陋”部分（如初始化/构造方法）是Python内建机制的核心，不应视为缺点。
• [CoolCold] 指出Python在Unix发行版中的集成优势，但认为Python的虚拟环境和版本管理复杂，尤其在跨版本运行时问题较多，需要依赖虚拟环境和容器等工具。
• [pyman] 回顾了Python的历史发展，指出其从系统管理员工具到被Google和Ubuntu采用，再到因大数据和机器学习兴起而广泛应用的过程，并提到过去编程语言间的“宗教战争”，认为现在开发者更务实。
• [Mawr] 对代码中的错误提示提出改进建议，认为应分别检查和提示缺失的变量，而不是用“OR”组合，以提高用户体验。
• [smcleod] 认为Python语言本身不错，但版本和包管理是个噩梦。
• [latexr] 对Python因AI火热而流行感到沮丧，认为这可能导致人们思维能力下降，并自愿 conform 到某种较低标准。
• [bravesoul2] 喜欢Python的语言特性，认为其在很多任务中足够好用，但包管理是个挑战，计划尝试新的工具。
• [firecall] 提问为何Python成为AI领域的主流语言。
• [t43562] 分享了自己从被迫使用Python到逐渐喜欢上它的经历，并对Make工具的使用提出看法。
• [Roark66] 分享了自己从Perl转向Python的经历，认为Python代码可读性好，尤其在团队环境中。
• [igor47] 赞同Python的改进，但认为async机制仍比其他语言痛苦，建议使用mise和just工具替代make。
• [DataDaoDe] 认为Python在打字和工具方面有显著改进，但async仍然是痛点，总体上因其丰富的库而在ML和数据处理领域表现出色。
• [flyinghamster] 长期避免使用Python，但因某些任务代码量少而开始使用，同时对“curl $URL | bash”这种安装方式表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• Python在不同操作系统（如Unix、BSD、macOS）上的默认安装情况讨论，[CoolCold] 和 [messe] 提到Python在不同系统中的集成情况有所不同。
• 对过去编程语言“宗教战争”的回顾，[pyman] 提到过去的语言之争，而现在开发者更注重实用性。
• 对AI推动Python流行的反思，[latexr] 对此趋势感到担忧，认为可能导致思维能力的下降。

争议焦点：
• Python的初始化/构造方法（如__init__、__new__）是否是“ legacy ugliness”的争论，[reedf1] 认为这是Python核心特性，而非缺点，但有人可能觉得这些机制复杂。
• 对Python包管理和虚拟环境复杂性的不满，[CoolCold] 和 [smcleod] 都提到Python包管理和版本控制的复杂性带来了挑战。

44579717.article_content:
I started to code more in
Python
around 6 months ago.
Why?
Because of AI, obviously.
It’s clear (to me) that big
money
opportunities are all over AI these days.
And guess what’s the
de facto
programming language for AI?
Yep, that sneaky one.
I had used Python before, but only for small scripts.
For example,
this script
scrapes metadata from all videos on
my YouTube channel
.
The metadata is dumped as
a JSON file
that I use to nicely display statistics of the videos
on this static page
.
As you can
see here
, this little script runs in solo mode every Monday via GitHub Actions.
Doing this kind of thing in Python is just way more convenient than, say, using Batch.
Not only because the syntax is more human-friendly, but also because the Python interpreter is natively integrated in all Unix distros.
Isn’t that cool?
So yeah, Python is powerful, and it couples very well with the now ubiquitous
VSCode
editor.
But I didn’t treat it seriously until recently,
1
it was just after I wanted to build AI applications (RAG, Agents, GenAI tools, etc.) for the “real world” that I realized that whether you like it or not, Python is the language of choice for that matters.
So I decided to give it a serious try, and to my great surprise, I’ve found that Python, and everything around it, has really improved a lot over the last decades.
Here’re just three examples:
Python has created a very complete ecosystem of libraries and tools for processing and analyzing data.
2
Python has gotten faster with optimized static compilers like
Cython
.
Python has done a good job of hiding its legacy ugliness (such as
__init__
,
__new__
, and similar aberrations), swettening its syntax to accomodate developers
with good taste
.
Thanks to this and many other things, I’m now feeling a particular joy for the language.
However, during this time, I’ve found that there’s still a big gap between using Python for “production-ready”
3
apps vs. the usual Jupyter notebook or script-based workflow.
So in this post, I share the tools, libraries, configs, and other integrations that bring me joy, and that I now use for building my Python applications.
⚠️ This post is highly biased toward the tools I personally use today, and if you think I’m missing some gem, please let me/us know (preferably in the comment section below).
Project Structure
I prefer to use a
monorepo
structure (backend and frontend) for my Python projects.
4
Why?
Because of my bad memory: I don’t like code parts scattered across multiple repositories (it’s definitely not search-friendly).
Because having multiple repost is mostly unnecessary: I’m just one guy, and I believe that if a project grows to the point that it needs to be split into multiple repositories, then it’s a sign of over-engineering.
Because I’m lazy: I like to keep things as simple as possible, compile, test, containerize, and deploy from a single location.
5
I would like to have a tool that generates the project structure for me, but I haven’t found one that fits me yet.
In the past, I used
CCDS
, a project initialization tool mostly for Data Science projects.
It’s very good, but it’s not targeting full-stack developers as its core users.
Here’s the typical structure of a project with a frontend-backend architecture (I’ll go through each subpart later in this post):
project/
│
├── .github/
# GitHub Actions workflows for CI/CD pipelines
│   ├── workflows/
# Directory containing YAML files for automated workflows
│   └── dependabot.yml
# Configuration for Dependabot to manage dependencies
│
├── .vscode/
# VSCode configuration for the project
│   ├── launch.json
# Debugging configurations for VSCode
│   └── settings.json
# Project-specific settings for VSCode
│
├── docs/
# Website and docs (a static SPA with MkDocs)
│
├── project-api/
# Backend API for handling business logic and heavy processing
│   ├── data/
# Directory for storing datasets or other static files
│   ├── notebooks/
# Jupyter notebooks for quick (and dirty) experimentation and prototyping
│   ├── tools/
# Utility scripts and tools for development or deployment
│   ├── src/
# Source code for the backend application
│   │   ├── app/
# Main application code
│   │   └── tests/
# Unit tests for the backend
│   │
│   ├── .dockerignore
# Specifies files to exclude from Docker builds
│   ├── .python-version
# Python version specification for pyenv
│   ├── Dockerfile
# Docker configuration for containerizing the backend
│   ├── Makefile
# Automation tasks for building, testing, and deploying
│   ├── pyproject.toml
# Python project configuration file
│   ├── README.md
# Documentation for the backend API
│   └── uv.lock
# Lock file for dependencies managed by UV
│
├── project-ui/
# Frontend UI for the project (Next.js, React, etc.)
│
├── .gitignore
# Global Git ignore file for the repository
├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
# Configuration for pre-commit hooks
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
# Guidelines for contributing to the project
├── docker-compose.yml
# Docker Compose configuratio

• Python在不同操作系统（如Unix、BSD、macOS）上的默认安装情况讨论，[CoolCold] 和 [messe] 提到Python在不同系统中的集成情况有所不同。
• 对过去编程语言“宗教战争”的回顾，[pyman] 提到过去的语言之争，而现在开发者更注重实用性。

• Python的初始化/构造方法（如__init__、__new__）是否是“ legacy ugliness”的争论，[reedf1] 认为这是Python核心特性，而非缺点，但有人可能觉得这些机制复杂。

data.title: High-resolution imaging method details nerves across a mouse’s body
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 研究人员使用高分辨率成像技术，绘制了从小鼠脑部和脊髓延伸至全身的神经网络，展示了单根神经纤维如何连接到远处器官。该方法利用化学处理使组织透明，并通过定制显微镜在40小时内快速扫描，成像深度达600微米。与以往耗时数月甚至数年的技术相比，该方法更快速高效。研究团队对16只成年小鼠进行了实验，使用不同标记技术标记神经子集，从而获得了详细的全身神经图谱。这一成果被视为连接组学领域的重大技术突破。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章中提到的技术流程及其创新性

不同观点：
• **Krisoft** 认为文章没有明确说明为了在切片时支撑组织，是否需要将组织冻结固化。他猜测可能是化学处理使样本变得坚固，并对这一技术细节表示疑问。
• **Krisoft** 还对流程中的创新点提出疑问，不确定创新是在于将切片机与显微镜集成，还是在于构建了一个比以往更快的设备。

补充讨论：
• **Krisoft** 对文章中未详细解释的技术细节表示关注，尤其是物理支撑和化学处理的具体作用。

总体来看，评论中的主要争议焦点在于技术流程的具体细节及其创新性。Krisoft对文章未详细说明关键步骤表示不满，并试图探讨该技术在领域中的新颖程度。

44564155.article_content:
Giant map details nerves across a mouse’s body: see stunning pics
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
The cranial nerves (blue) and blood vessels (red) in the head of a mouse are revealed by a high-resolution imaging technique.
Credit: M.-Y. Shi
et al./Cell
(
CC-BY-4.0
)
A speedy imaging method can map the nerves running from a mouse’s brain and spinal cord to the rest of its body at micrometre-scale resolution, revealing details such as individual fibres travelling from a key nerve to distant organs
1
.
Previous efforts have mapped
the network of connections between nerve cells, known as the connectome, in the mouse brain
. But tracing the complex paths of nerves through the rest of the body has been challenging. To do so, the creators of the new map used a custom-built microscope to scan exposed tissue, completing the process in just 40 hours.
Nerves look blue in the reconstructed view of a genetically engineered mouse (left) whose neurons produce a fluorescent marker. In a separate animal (right), antibodies detail the sympathetic nerves (purple).
Credit: M.-Y. Shi
et al./Cell
(
CC-BY-4.0
)
The method, described today in
Cell
, is an important technical achievement, says Ann-Shyn Chiang, a neuroscientist at the National Tsing Hua University in Hsinchu, Taiwan, who was not involved with the research. “This work is a major step forward in expanding connectomics beyond the brain,” he says.
Clearing the way
To prepare a mouse’s body for the scan, researchers treat it with chemicals that make its tissues transparent by removing fat, calcium and other components that block light. This provides a clear view of the nerves, which have been labelled with fluorescent marker proteins. The see-through body is then placed into a device that combines a slicing tool and a microscope that takes 3D images.
A piston gradually pushes the mouse towards the slicing blade, 400 micrometres at a time. After each slice, a microscope images the newly exposed surface of the mouse, capturing details up to 600 micrometres deep — roughly the thickness of six sheets of paper — below the surface. The body then advances for the next cut. The cycle repeats around 200 times without pause, to cover the entire body. The images are then combined.
Sympathetic nerves (green) can be seen branching through the outer layer of the kidney thanks to antibody labelling of proteins in nerve cells.
Credit: M.-Y. Shi
et al./Cell
(
CC-BY-4.0
)
The authors say the method is much faster than other techniques, which require frequent pauses. “A slower system would take months or years, increasing the chance of mechanical failure, signal loss or sample degradation,” says co-author Guoqiang Bi, a neuroscientist at the University of Science and Technology of China in Hefei.
Mouse with a glow
Researchers repeated the process on 16 adult mice, using three distinct marking techniques to label subsets of nerves.

data.title: The reality of firearm suppressors vs. Hollywood
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了枪械消音器的实际效果，澄清了电影如《约翰·威克》中对消音器的夸张描绘。作者指出，即使使用消音器，枪声依然非常响亮，仅能降低部分噪音，远不能达到完全静音的效果。文章详细解释了枪声的组成：机械声、音爆和枪口冲击波，并通过分贝对比表说明不同枪械的噪音水平。例如，AT4无后座力反坦克武器的噪音高达187分贝，而使用消音器后，.22步枪的噪音仍可达140分贝。文章还提到，消音器的主要优点是保护听力和减少枪口火焰，但其效果和使用范围有限，并非所有枪械都适用。最后，作者呼吁读者点赞、订阅并分享文章，以支持其内容创作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： Hollywood 电影中枪械消音器的表现是否真实，以及与现实中枪械声音的差异。

不同观点：
• **[saltcured的观点]**：Hollywood 对声音的处理具有高度的风格化，音频再现的动态范围有限，导致声音效果并不追求真实。例如，电影中的低语在现实中不可能在嘈杂的剧院后排被听到。同时，电影中的声音效果已经成为一种符号化的代码，而非真实反映。比如，Hollywood 中的鞋、饮料、衣服和性行为的声音都与现实不符。此外，旧的音响系统也限制了真实声音的再现，枪声在电影中已经被“消音”处理以适应播放环境，这导致需要进一步简化声音以使其区别于其他声音。

• **[idrathernot的观点]**：作为枪械爱好者，基于实际体验，他提到在现实中使用消音器确实能显著降低枪声，虽然不如电影中那么安静，但消音器与高质量子弹结合使用时，能有效保护听力并使射击体验更舒适。他指出，消音后的枪声更低沉，且没有超音速弹药的刺耳声。

• **[tstrimple的观点]**：tstrimple 认为，枪械爱好者在不同场合对消音器的描述存在不一致。他们在对外时会强调消音器只是为了保护听力，而在内部讨论时却会夸耀能将枪械变得“Hollywood 安静”。此外，Hollywood 在表现消音武器时，最误导人的不仅是枪声本身，还有子弹撞击目标的声音，后者在现实中往往比枪声更响亮。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Hollywood 对枪声的表现是否误导观众，以及现实中消音器的效果与电影中的差距。枪械爱好者之间对消音器效果的描述也存在不一致，部分人认为电影夸大了消音效果，而另一部分人则认为在特定条件下可以实现接近电影中的效果。

• **例子和论据**：
  - saltcured 提到了电影声音风格化和符号化的例子，以及 Dirty Harry 电影中对枪声的艺术化处理。
  - idrathernot 通过个人经验说明了消音器在现实中的效果，并提供了实际使用消音器的例子。
  - tstrimple 提供了 YouTube 视频链接以支持其观点，并指出了 Hollywood 在表现消音武器时子弹撞击声的误导性。

这些讨论展示了电影艺术化处理与现实体验之间的显著差异，以及枪械爱好者在不同语境下对消音器效果的不同描述。

44578181.article_content:
The reality of firearm suppressors.
June 12, 2025
16 minutes
Hello again. I’m going to stick on the topic of intermediate ballistics this week, but go into a bit more detail on silencers/suppressors
1
. I hinted last week that I might go on a deep dive, and I’ve had a few questions about silencers, so let’s strike while the iron (or gun barrel) is hot.
As this post’s title suggests, we’ll debunk the myth created by Hollywood that a firearm can be completely silenced, reduced only to a “pew”. I’ll pull together some examples of silenced firearms and show what silencers/suppressors can and can’t do, and compare the noises you’d get to some other types of sound. Then I’ll go into the components which make up firearm noise: mechanical, sonic boom, and muzzle blast. Then I’ll discuss the advantages that silencers bring, even though they’re not as impressive as they seem in the movies. Finally, I’ll sum up by discussing the limitations of silencers and why they are not universal.
I included this clip from
John Wick: Chapter 2
in last week’s post, but I didn’t give it the attention it deserved as a truly ridiculous piece of cinema. Really, it deserves its own post just
like I did with
The Expendables
, it’s that ridiculous, but instead we’ll use it as an anchor for today’s discussion while we also pull in some other Hollywood examples. Thankfully for us, there’s no shortage of unrealistic silencers on screen. Here’s the John Wick clip again:
This warrants another entry in the Realism vs. Drama Hall of Fame:
This is probably a bit on the generous side for John Wick, but he’s in exalted company. I often read about how realistic the “gunplay” in these movies is, as if that wasn’t an oxymoron. The director has the right idea:
it’s comic book action
.
One thing I won’t be silent about is my usual request for you to “like,” subscribe, and share this post if you’ve enjoyed it. There’s a handy subscription link below. It really helps. Please also comment below if you want to join in the conversation. Alternatively you can contact me via
webform here
or
email here
.
Type your email…
Subscribe
<< Bullets flying backwards
Send in the troops (Part 1) >>
Even a quieter gunshot is still very loud
Gunshots are very loud things, so even when you eliminate most of their noise, they’re still loud. Last week
I mentioned decibels
, which are the unit of measurement of sound intensity level (i.e. loudness). Here’s a chart (you can find any number
like this on Google
) which compares the decibel level of some common things:
Please take this with a grain of salt. Sounds vary depending on how close you are, and no distances are specified here.
Decibels are a funny unit, designed to measure the wide range of sound pressure levels that correspond to loudness. For example, 180 dB is a billion billion times louder than 0 dB
2
. I don’t know about you, but I can’t picture a billion billion anything. To make matters more complicated, our ears
don’t respond in a linear way
to sound pressure. It’s like they have their own algorithm in there to make sense of the world (your brain, I suppose). All you need to know is that:
An increase of 10 dB is ten times louder, but sounds twice as loud
A decrease of 10 dB is ten times quieter, but sounds half as loud
An increase of 3 dB is a doubling in loudness, but is the smallest increase in volume we can perceive
A decrease of 3 dB is a halving in loudness, but is the smallest decrease in volume we can perceive
We see that “explosion” tops out the scale in the chart above, at 150 dB. How does this compare with gunshots? The loudness of a weapon (or anything) depends on the strength of the pressure wave and how close the listener is to the source. The problem with the above chart is that there are no distances, but we do have
some firearms data
which is calibrated to an observer 1 m away from the gun:
Firing a…
…registers…
AT4
recoilless anti-tank weapon
187 dB (
according to this
source). Might be measured closer than 1 m.
Smith & Wesson 586
.357 Magnum pistol
169 dB
Remington 742
rifle (.30-06 calibre, standard 22″ barrel)
161.6 dB
Remington SP-10 10-gauge shotgun
161.4 dB
Glock 22
.40 pistol
159 dB
AR-15
5.56mm rifle
158.9 dB
.22 rifle
140 dB (no distance specified,
this source
).
For some context to these numbers, 187 dB feels 20 to 130 times louder than the pain threshold of hearing (115-140 dB). 160 dB feels more than twice as loud (and is actually more like 10x as loud) as the top of most decibel charts. 140 dB is the level above which
hearing protection is mandatory
in the workplace, no matter how short the exposure it.
So much for unsilenced firearms. What difference does a silencer make? Dakota Silencer (now known as
Silencer Central
) produced a handy graphic comparing the difference between unsuppressed and suppressed versions of common firearms
3

company link here

data.title: North Korean XORIndex malware hidden in 67 malicious NPM packages
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 北韩威胁行为者在npm存储库中植入了67个恶意软件包，用于传播名为XORIndex的新型恶意软件加载器，这些包已被下载超过17,000次。这些软件包伪装成合法项目，如"vite-meta-plugin"等，安装后执行后门程序，收集主机数据并发送至命令与控制服务器。XORIndex与之前的HexEval Loader并行使用，最终部署BeaverTail和InvisibleFerret后门，用于数据窃取和进一步攻击。研究人员警告，这些攻击者不断变换手法以逃避检测，建议开发者仔细检查软件包来源，并在隔离环境中测试新库以确保安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：npm包的安全性以及其可能被恶意利用的问题

44579931.article_content:
North Korean XORIndex malware hidden in 67 malicious npm packages
By
Bill Toulas
July 15, 2025
01:47 PM
0
North Korean threat actors planted 67 malicious packages in the Node Package Manager (npm) online repository to deliver a new malware loader called XORIndex to developer systems.
The packages collectively count more than 17,000 downloads and were discovered by researchers at package security platform Socket, who assess them to be part of the continued Contagious Interview operation.
Socket researchers say that the campaign follows threat activity detected since April. Last month, the same actor infiltrated npm with
35 packages
that dropped information stealers and backdoors onto developers’ devices.
Timeline of the latest attack waves
Source: Socket
Overview of the attacks
Contagious Interview
is a North Korean state-backed campaign that targets mostly developers with fake job offers to trick them into running malicious code on their systems.
The purpose varies from collecting sensitive information that allows breaching companies to stealing cryptocurrency assets.
The Node Package Manager (npm) is the default package manager for Node.js, a platform where developers publish and install JavaScript libraries and tools. It is widely used in web development, but also frequently exploited by threat actors for malware distribution.
Out of the 67 packages the threat actors uploaded onto npm this time, there are several that appear to mimic or blend the names of legitimate software projects and libraries, like:
vite-meta-plugin
vite-postcss-tools
vite-logging-tool
vite-proc-log
pretty-chalk
postcss-preloader
js-prettier
flowframe
figwrap
midd-js, middy-js
When victims install any of these packages, a ‘postinstall’ script executes to launch XORIndex Loader, a novel tool that appears to be used in parallel with HexEval Loader, a malware dropper observed in past attacks.
XORIndex Loader collects host data to profile each victim and sends it to a hardcoded command and control (C2) address, hosted on infrastructure from Vercel cloud application company.
The C2 server responds with one or more JavaScript payloads, which are executed on the victim’s system using eval(). These payloads are typically the BeaverTail and the InvisibleFerret backdoor, both attributed to North Korean Contagious Interview operations.
The two pieces of malware provide access to compromised machines, allow data exfiltration, and can download more payloads.
According to the researchers, the North Korean hackers blend old and new tools with subtle modifications to evade detection, and every time npm cleans an infection, they return via different npm accounts and package names.
“Contagious Interview threat actors will continue to diversify their malware portfolio, rotating through new npm maintainer aliases, reusing loaders such as HexEval Loader and malware families like BeaverTail and InvisibleFerret, and actively deploying newly observed variants including XORIndex Loader” - Socket
“Defenders should expect continued iterations of these loaders across newly published packages, often with slight variations to evade detection,” the researchers warn.
Socket researchers say that they reported to npm all malicious packages from the latest campaign but some of them may still be available in the repository.
It is important to double-check sourced packages to ensure they’re not typosquatting decoys, only trust well-known projects and publishers with a proven record, and scrutinize recent repository activity for signs of automation.
When possible, always examine the source code for obfuscation and execute new libraries in isolated environments to evaluate their safety.
8 Common Threats in 2025
While cloud attacks may be growing more sophisticated, attackers still succeed with surprisingly simple techniques.
Drawing from Wiz's detections across thousands of organizations, this report reveals 8 key techniques used by cloud-fluent threat actors.
Get the Report

Dozens of malicious packages on NPM collect host and network data
North Korean hackers deepfake execs in Zoom call to spread Mac malware

data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种新的闪电探测器电路，使用单感应线圈调谐接收约200 kHz的静电脉冲，通过高输入阻抗的达林顿晶体管RF放大器简化设计，整个电路仅消耗约200 µA电流，使用两节D型碱性电池供电。该电路的地闪部分设计与早期版本类似，但晶体管极性相反，输出脉冲从高电平短暂降至地电平。文中提供了详细的电路图和近照，以便初学者理解。文中还提到可通过调整电位器来增加灵敏度控制，建议在室外或靠近窗户使用，并连接良好地线以提高灵敏度。文章最后讨论了元件选择和布局建议，强调了电路不特别挑剔元件，但经验有助于更好地理解和组装。

• **[panki27]** 分享了一个实时、社区来源的闪电地图网站（Blitzortung.org），但表示之前分享过但没有引起关注。这表明他关注的是一种更依赖于社区参与和共享数据的闪电监测方式。

• **[JKCalhoun]** 提到了一种非常简易的闪电检测器，由天线、氖灯和接地线组成，并分享了一个改进该设计的链接。他认为这种简单的设计虽然看似不起作用，但实际上是可以工作的，并对这种简单技术的有效性表示惊讶。

• 争议的焦点：不同用户对闪电检测技术的复杂性和实用性有不同的看法。**[bri3d]** 和 **[JKCalhoun]** 分别介绍了现代集成电路和简易自制设备，展示了技术实现的多样性。**[Arch-TK]** 对某种原型制作方法提出质疑，反映了在技术实现细节上的不同意见。

• 社区参与和数据共享： **[panki27]**、 **[anoynmoose]** 和 **[ortusdux]** 都提到了社区参与和数据共享的重要性，展示了用户对集体智慧和合作项目的关注。

• 实际应用和创意： **[rkagerer]** 提出的问题引导了关于闪电传感器实际应用的讨论，鼓励用户思考和分享创意想法。

New Lightning Detector

Also:
Original Lightning Detector

To observe the lightning strikes on a map in near real time
try:
https://www.iweathernet.com/lightning/latest-lightning-strikes-on-google-maps
The latency is usually under 10 seconds but that's long enough
to make correlation with a flash from your detector with a flash on the map a
bit challenging.
Built to make the wiring easy to follow, but I prefer this
circuit to the original. Read the text below.
This new lightning detector circuit uses a single inductor tuned
circuit to receive static pulses from lightning at a frequency near 200 kHz. The
need for a tapped tuned circuit is eliminated by employing a very high input
impedance RF amplifier that uses a darlington transistor. The amplifier is
micro-power and the whole circuit draws only about 200 uA from two alkaline D
cells, hardly denting the shelf life. The flasher portion of the circuit is
similar to the earlier versions only the polarity of the transistors is
reversed. As a result the output pulses momentarily go to ground from a
normally-high state.
The schematic and close-up photos were made with the beginner in
mind. Questions about the schematic can be answered by close-up examination of
the photos. Try a magnifier utility for an even closer look.
The 150k resistor in the base of the 2N4401 may be
replaced with a series combination of a 100k resistor and a 100k (or greater)
potentiometer to add sensitivity control. Simply adjust the potentiometer until
flashing just stops for maximum sensitivity. The fixed resistor is plenty
sensitive for most users. But, the receiver will only work well outside or near
a window. A few yards of wire could be used to run an antenna out a window but
connect a 47 pF capacitor in series with the wire at the detector end. Also, connecting a good ground will improve the sensitivity. Keep the unit away from electronic or electrical appliances and
wiring for best performance.
A common mistake is to select a 10 uH choke instead of a 10 mH.
The large green choke in the photo is typical of the size and markings to
expect. Color bands are brown, black, orange. A wide silver band often indicates
the beginning of the color code.
Some of the other parts in the prototype were chosen to make it
easy for the beginner to see the values. For example, the large .1 uF "orange
drop" can be a tiny ceramic type. Parts may be in odd positions, too. The orange 10 uF is twisted to make the markings visible and
other parts are oriented to make viewing easy.
The 100 uF shown across the battery is the blue part right below
the MPSA63 in the photo below. Notice how it isn't right by the battery
connections. Sometimes the position of a component relative to others is
important but that information is often not on a schematic unless specifically
stated. Schematics aren't usually physical representations; they just show which
legs of the various parts are electrically connected. Schematics are usually
accompanied by assembly drawings as part of a complete design especially when
layout is critical. The point is to not take schematics to be mechanical layout
instructions although they often are a fairly good start. On the other hand
schematics generally aren't intentionally misleading about a good location for
the part but a little electronics experience helps a great deal when
there's only a schematic to go by.
The parts are not particularly critical. The darlington PNP
transistor may be a different number, as may the other transistors. The diodes can
be any silicon switching diode, like the 1N4448 (or probably any orange one you
have). An amber LED with a 22 ohm resistor draws about 30 mA with fresh
batteries. Vary the resistor to achieve the desired LED current for other colors
(connect the LED and resistor to the battery through a current meter to select
the value). The output transistor can sink several hundred mA, so several LEDs or
other loads may be connected in parallel. The head from a cheap LED flahslight that uses two
cells will be really bright! The pulse is pretty short to save power and for
quick response, but for longer pulses, increase the 10 uF capacitor value. You
might want a longer pulse to flash a 3 volt incandescent bulb (my favorite).
Actually, I'm using a 1.5 volt bulb and it's really bright (not shown in the
photos), even with this short pulse! I have lots of them and I'm sure I'll need
to replace it fairly often.
Below is a close-up with the sensitivity
adjustment option and an incandescent bulb. The construction technique was chosen to make it easy to
follow the wiring. Normally, the leads would be stuck through the holes and
wired on the other side of the perf board. I used the perf board simply as a
guide for copper nails driven into a pine board - strictly to make it easy to
see all the connections.  The perf board serves no purpose beyond
visibility, so one could also us

• 争议的焦点：不同用户对闪电检测技术的复杂性和实用性有不同的看法。**[bri3d]** 和 **[JKCalhoun]** 分别介绍了现代集成电路和简易自制设备，展示了技术实现的多样性。**[Arch-TK]** 对某种原型制作方法提出质疑，反映了在技术实现细节上的不同意见。

• 社区参与和数据共享： **[panki27]**、 **[anoynmoose]** 和 **[ortusdux]** 都提到了社区参与和数据共享的重要性，展示了用户对集体智慧和合作项目的关注。

• 实际应用和创意： **[rkagerer]** 提出的问题引导了关于闪电传感器实际应用的讨论，鼓励用户思考和分享创意想法。

data.title: Thunderbird: Fluent Windows 11 Design
data.author: skipnup
data.article_summary: FluentBird是一款为Mozilla Thunderbird设计的userChrome.css主题，实现了Windows 11的Fluent Design和Mica透明材质效果。该主题支持亮色和暗色模式，增强了Thunderbird在Windows 11系统上的视觉体验。最新版本0.1.5修复了暗模式下的信封图形问题，并解决了卡片视图中主题冲突等问题。安装需启用userChrome.css，并将相关文件复制到Thunderbird的配置目录中。由于是测试版，仍存在一些未完成的样式和已知问题，如无法完全主题化所有元素。该项目基于MIT许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Thunderbird应用的设计美观性与实用性之间的平衡，以及功能性问题。

不同观点：
• ttoinou：认为Thunderbird的基本设计虽然不美观，但非常实用，适合长时间使用，且有效减少眼睛疲劳。强调功能性和效率优于美观。
• paintbox：对搜索栏的位置感到不满，认为其浪费了宝贵的空间，并提到浏览器设计经过多年迭代才达到目前的状态，建议将经验应用到邮件客户端上。
• huhtenberg、bluedino：批评设计中有过多的空白和低信息密度，尤其在拥有高分辨率屏幕的情况下，只能看到少量邮件。
• accrual：赞赏"Fluent"设计的美学，尤其是半透明效果，并希望看到更多早期玻璃效果设计的回归，但也提到搜索栏设计不佳。
• tummler：对Thunderbird整体性能不满，尤其是下载邮件数据时的设置问题，认为即使主题美观，软件本身仍有待改进。

补充讨论：
• ape4：澄清“fluent”在此处指的是Microsoft设计风格，而非编程中的流畅接口。
• Calzifer：讨论了Thunderbird在使用userChrome.css自定义主题时的一些技术限制和解决方案，特别是涉及Shadow DOM的样式修改。
• neogodless：关注主题在实际使用场景中的表现，希望看到在大量文件夹存在时主题的视觉效果。
• hammyhavoc：询问是否有支持Gmail外部账户和签名功能的扩展，强调了Thunderbird在此方面的不足。
• AdmiralAsshat：提到Thunderbird的主题Monterail，虽然视觉效果好，但缺乏进一步的发展和更新。
• guluarte、thesuitonym：不希望Thunderbird看起来像Outlook，认为主题设计不应模仿Outlook。
• hk1337：对Thunderbird仍在更新表示惊讶，并提到Windows 11设计在macOS上的不协调。
• kookamamie：对Thunderbird是否仍然存在可能删除或损坏所有邮件的bug表示担忧。

争议焦点：
• 设计美观性与实用性的权衡：一部分用户认为Thunderbird的设计虽然不美观，但非常实用，适合长时间使用；另一部分用户则对低信息密度和过多空白表示不满，认为设计可以更紧凑。
• Thunderbird的功能性问题：部分用户对Thunderbird的性能和功能（如邮件下载设置、外部账户支持等）提出质疑，认为即使主题美观，软件本身的改进更为重要。
• 主题风格的方向：一些用户不希望Thunderbird模仿Outlook的设计风格，认为其应该保持独特性。

FluentBird
FluentBird is a userChrome.css theme for Mozilla Thunderbird, that implemenets Windows 11 Fluent Design and Mica transparency materials.
Created by Danny King -
www.dannyking.co.uk
Released under the MIT License
Features
Implements Fluent Design styling in Thunderbird
Supports both dark and light modes (system theme)
Enhances and highlights Mica transparency on Windows 11 systems
This will likely be the last beta release, unless more issues are raised, with 1.0 release to occur alongside Thunderbird 141.
0.1.5 Release Notes
Improves the "no messages" envolope graphic in dark mode.
Fixes the subject line clashing with the star / tags icons in card view.
0.1.4 Release Notes
Adds Fluent icons and correct button styling for the "Reply List" button
Fixes button hover colour in Dark Mode
Fixes subject line colour on card view in Dark Mode
Credits
FluentBird uses Fluent Design icons provided by Microsoft, licensed under the MIT License.
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
Setup Instructions
Enable userChrome.css
Open Thunderbird
Go to
Settings
>
General
Click
Config Editor…
under
Advanced
Search for
toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets
Set it to
true
Restart Thunderbird
Enable the Mica flags in Thunderbird’s (Firefox-based) advanced configuration:
Open Thunderbird
Go to
Settings
>
General
Scroll down and click
Config Editor…
under
Advanced
In the search bar, type
widget.windows.mica
and set it to
true
Search for
widget.windows.mica.popups
and set it to
2
Make sure no other theme is selected in Thunderbird settings.
Do not
select Light, Dark, or any theme from the Thunderbird extension store.
The theme must be set to "System Theme" or simply unselected.
Copy the included files to the
chrome
folder in your Thunderbird profile directory:
Click on Help > Troubleshooting information
Scroll down to "Profile Folder" under "Application Basics" and click "Open Folder"
Create a new folder named
chrome
inside your profile folder, if it does not already exist
Place the userChrome.css file and all folders into the 'chrome' directory
Restart Thunderbird.
Known Issues
This is a beta release. Expect bugs and incomplete styling.
Untested on Mac and Linux (should work, but without Mica).
Report issues via the GitHub repository.
Also, note that some areas of ThunderBird are rendered outside of the influence of userChrome.css in a "Shadow DOM" - as such, it is not possible to fully theme all elements of Thunderbird.
The mail section is fully themed, as is the general window chrome. The Contacts, Calendar, Tasks and Chat functions have limited themeing in some areas.
It isn't possible to style the new message / reply message window, or any other pop-up windows.
As they are entirely contained within a Shadow DOM, it is also not possible to theme the settings areas.
Questions?
Check the GitHub repo or open an issue there. Enjoy!

data.author: marcodiego

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux桌面操作系统使用增长的原因及相关争议

不同观点：
• **Linux增长原因的讨论**：
  - **nerdjon**：怀疑Linux增长是因为整体桌面计算机数量下降，而非Linux本身使用增加。他认为技术用户继续使用Linux，而非技术用户转向手机和平板。
  - **palata**：认为Linux增长部分是由于游戏支持的改善（如Steam Deck）以及隐私关注增加。
  - **theandrewbailey**：在电子废物回收公司工作，提到通过翻新电脑推广Linux，但不确定用户是否继续使用。

• **数据可靠性争议**：
  - **jsnell**：质疑统计数据的可靠性，指出Statcounter数据曾出现明显错误，如经典Mac OS使用率突然上升。
  - **dosinga**：认为长期来看，数据波动很大，误差范围可能很大。

• **Linux使用体验与用户界面问题**：
  - **Workaccount2**：批评Linux的用户界面，尤其是命令行界面的复杂性，认为这是阻碍其普及的原因。
  - **mousethatroared**：认为浏览器和办公软件的跨平台支持使Linux成为可行的桌面操作系统。

• **其他因素的讨论**：
  - **andyferris**：质疑AI训练网络爬虫所使用的操作系统，对Linux市场份额数据持怀疑态度。
  - **ryandv**：认为Linux应保持当前的采用水平，避免因大众化而导致质量下降。
  - **taf2**：以个人经验为例，认为Linux在游戏方面表现优异。
  - **schmudde**：认为浏览器应用模式的兴起降低了Windows API的重要性。
  - **lvl155**：认为Linux发行版的多样性分散了桌面环境开发的努力，影响其普及。

补充讨论：
- **Steam Deck的影响**：多个评论提到Steam Deck对Linux使用率的贡献，但对其能否持续增长存在不同看法。
- **Windows 11的影响**：有评论认为Linux增长可能部分是由于Windows 11表现不佳。

争议焦点：
- **Linux使用率增长的真实性**：数据可靠性和统计方法的争议是讨论的核心，部分评论者质疑数据是否准确反映实际情况。
- **Linux桌面操作系统的易用性**：用户界面的复杂性被认为是限制Linux普及的重要因素，尤其是对非技术用户而言。

data.title: Pixel Piranhas
data.author: spython
data.article_summary: 文章描述了作者在网络上看到糟糕新闻时的无力感，尽管与自己无关，但仍感到这些事不该发生。这种情境下，作者有种想立即做出反应的冲动，类似于想把报纸揉皱扔掉，但在屏幕上却无法表达不满。为此，作者开发了一个浏览器扩展程序，点击按钮后，网页会被一群像饥饿食人鱼般的光标慢慢撕碎。文章末尾提供了在Firefox和Chrome上安装的链接，并附带了一些相关的科技主题和订阅选项。

不同观点：

• [waltbosz] 联想到一个名为 face.com 的早期DOS程序（1980年代末），描述了该程序如何在文本控制台上显示字符并与用户互动，提到了两个有趣的控制功能（聚集和跳舞），进一步佐证早期“玩具应用”的存在。
• [OneFriend2575] 认为这种程序表面上是愚蠢的乐趣，但具有更深层的意义，例如重新获得控制权和改变对网络内容的感受，指出这种互动可以影响用户对网络环境的情感反应。
• [jihadjihad] 以一种幽默的方式评论MrBeast被数字食人鱼吞噬，带有诗意的隐喻，可能暗示对名人或网络文化的某种看法。
• [Stevemiller07] 对“Pixel Piranhas”程序表现出兴趣，询问其是否为开源或仍在早期访问阶段，显示出对该程序技术状态的关注。
• [poulpy123] 以调侃的方式评论该程序比“打屏幕”更省钱，表现出对压力释放方式的幽默理解。

补充讨论：
• 该讨论中涉及到早期计算机程序的历史，特别是DOS时代的玩具应用，展示了这类程序的演变。
• 部分评论者如[OneFriend2575]深入探讨了这种程序的心理和情感影响，提出了对用户界面自定义的新视角。
• 争议的焦点可能在于这种程序的价值和意义，一些人认为其仅为娱乐，另一些人如[OneFriend2575]则看到了更深层次的象征意义。

I really hate it when I’m  exposed to some horrible news online, and feel powerless. There is nothing I can do, I am not responsible, and yet at the same time I have this feeling “this shouldn’t be happening”.
There is a temptation to immediately react â if it was printed, I would crumple up the paper and throw it away â yet, reading pixels on the screen I don’t have the right gesture to express my discontent.
So I made this little browser extension. Click on a button, and a horde of cursors, like hungry piranhas, will slowly rip the web page apart for you.

data.title: MARS.EXE → COM (2021)
data.author: reconnecting
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了1993年由Tim J. Clarke编写的火星景观渲染器代码，对其进行了详细分析和研究。原始的MARS.EXE文件大小为5649字节，作者对其进行反汇编、重写和优化，将其压缩至1517字节。文章提供了原始代码和优化后的MARS.COM代码，并详细说明了转换过程和算法。此外，文章还介绍了如何使用DEBUG工具提取和解析二进制数据，同时提醒操作时需谨慎。作者尝试联系原作者Tim未果，希望他能看到此文并取得联系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕经典DOS演示程序MARS.EXE及其技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• **对MARS.EXE的赞赏与怀旧**：
  - [reconnecting] 提到第一次在386电脑上看到MARS.EXE，认为其在实时图形处理上的成就如同魔法。
  - [Andrew_nenakhov] 表达了对MARS.EXE的怀旧情感，提到很久没有听到这个名称。
  - [baal80spam] 对比现代软件（如Windows 11的记事本）的大小，突显MARS.EXE在文件大小上的精简。

• **技术实现与历史背景**：
  - [reconnecting] 引用pouet.net上的描述，介绍了MARS.EXE由Tim Clarke在1993年编写，因其高效的实时分形地形渲染而获得传奇地位，并提到其对作者职业生涯的影响。
  - [amiga386] 关注MARS.EXE在真实386机器上的表现，质疑在现代多GHz机器上通过DOSBox模拟运行的效果。

• **个人经历与技术挑战**：
  - [nickdothutton] 分享了童年时购买分形书籍并尝试在z80家用电脑上重现分形图形的经历。
  - [phkahler] 回忆了自己在学校时阅读MARS.EXE的技术描述并用Turbo Pascal在486上实现了自己的版本。

• **技术比较与未来可能性**：
  - [kragen] 提出MARS.EXE是否预见了Comanche游戏中的Voxel Space 3-D渲染算法的问题，引发对技术演进的思考。
  - [flockonus] 表达了希望通过WASM等技术在网页上运行MARS.EXE的愿望。
  - [tetris11] 提到寻找可以在线运行DOSBox并加载ASM的工具，但未找到合适的选项。

• **对程序细节的探索**：
  - [shmerl] 提到曾在二进制编辑器中查看MARS.EXE，并发现一个字节可以改变颜色调色板。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的相关资源，如cdak演示和Springer Verlag的分形书籍，为理解MARS.EXE的技术背景提供了额外信息。
• 讨论中涉及的技术细节（如Voxel Space 3-D渲染算法）和现代技术（如WASM）展示了经典程序在当代技术环境中的潜在应用。

争议焦点：
• MARS.EXE在现代系统上的表现是否与其在原始386硬件上的表现一致，是讨论中的一个争议点，特别是在使用DOSBox模拟运行的情况下。

data.title: Show HN: HN v0.2.1 – Native macOS app for reading HN
data.author: 120-dev
data.article_summary: 120 HN 是一款用于阅读和互动 Hacker News 内容的本地应用，专为科技和创业新闻设计。它通过人工智能技术提供智能内容总结和评论分析，帮助用户快速了解文章和讨论的重点及社区观点。应用支持 macOS（Apple 芯片和 Intel 芯片），Linux 和 Windows 版本即将推出。用户可免费使用，或通过输入优惠码获得免费许可。应用功能包括原生 Hacker News 阅读、支持自定义 API 密钥、本地大语言模型、网页内容总结及讨论分析等。

data.title: ICE may deport to 'third countries' without assurances they won't be tortured
data.author: perihelions
data.article_summary: 美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）发布了一份备忘录，允许在某些紧急情况下将移民驱逐到与其无联系的国家，即使这些移民可能面临迫害或酷刑风险。根据该备忘录，如果美国国务院认为目的地国家提供的外交保证可信，移民可以在六小时内被驱逐，无需进一步程序。通常情况下，移民会收到至少24小时的通知，并有机会与律师交谈。然而，批评者认为该政策无视法律和宪法要求，外交保证不充分且不透明，且时间过短，移民难以评估风险。国土安全部则称这些协议确保了正当程序，对国家安全至关重要。

A U.S. Air Force Boeing C-17 used for deportation flights is pictured at Biggs Army Airfield in Fort Bliss, El Paso, Texas on Feb. 13.
Justin hamel / AFP via Getty Images file
July 15, 2025, 8:30 PM EDT
By
Daniella Silva
and
Didi Martinez
The Trump administration may deport immigrants to a country where they have no connections, in some cases with as little as six hours' notice and without assurances from the destination country that the deported individuals “will not be persecuted or tortured,” according to a new memo from a top immigration official.
The Immigration and Customs Enforcement memo, which says the policy is "effective immediately," was issued July 9 by acting Director Todd Lyons. It provides guidance to ICE employees on how to deport people to countries other than their country of origin and, “in exigent circumstances,” even if there's a risk they will be persecuted or tortured there.
“If the United States has received diplomatic assurances from the country of removal that aliens removed from the United States will not be persecuted or tortured, and if the Department of State believes those assurances to be credible, the alien may be removed without the need for further procedures,” said the memo, which was
first reported by The Washington Post
and became public Tuesday in court filings.
Lyons wrote that “in all other cases” where the United States has not received those assurances, ICE must comply with several procedures, including that an ICE officer will serve the immigrant with a notice of removal that lists what country the federal government intends to deport them to in a language that the immigrant understands; will not affirmatively ask whether the person is afraid of being sent to that country; and will wait at least 24 hours before removing the person from the U.S.
But “in exigent circumstances,” Lyons wrote, the officer may deport the person in as little as six hours as long as the person is “provided reasonable means and opportunity to speak with an attorney.”
Immigrants who could be subject to the policy include those who have been given final orders of removal but in which a judge has found they would still be at risk of persecution or torture if deported from the Unites States,
as well as those who come from countries where the U.S. lacks diplomatic relations or an established ability to send deportees to those countries, such as Cuba.
Though ICE officers are told not to ask migrants if they are afraid of deportation to a third country, those who do state such a fear will will be referred for screening for possible protection within 24 hours, according to the memo. That screening could lead to the migrant being referred to immigration court for further proceedings or ICE possibly trying to send them to a different country than they one which they express fear of being deported to.
Trina Realmuto, the executive director of the National Immigration Litigation Alliance, which is involved in a federal lawsuit challenging the deportations of migrants to countries other than their own, said in a statement to NBC News that the memo establishes a policy that “blatantly disregards the requirements required by statute, regulation, and the Constitution.”
She said the memo means there will be “no process whatsoever when the government claims to have credible diplomatic assurances” for immigrants who are to be deported to third countries. Those assurances, she added, “are unlawful” because they don't protect deportees from persecution or torture at the hands of non-state actors and because they violate legal requirements establishing that they be individualized and that migrants have the chance to review and rebut them.
Realmuto also criticized the government for not publicly sharing what countries it has obtained diplomatic assurances from and what those countries got in exchange.
The rest of the policy is “woefully deficient,” she said.
“It provides a mere between 6- and 24-hours’ notice before deportation to a third country, which is simply not enough time for any person to assess whether they would be persecuted or tortured in that third country, especially if they don’t know anything about the country or don’t have a lawyer,” Realmuto said.
In a statement to NBC News on Tuesday, before the memo became public, the Department of Homeland Security said the agency has “successfully negotiated nearly a dozen safe third country agreements.”
“If countries aren’t receiving their own citizens, other countries have agreed that they would take them. It is incredibly important to make sure we get these worst of the worst criminal illegal aliens out of our country,” Assistant Secretary Tricia McLaughlin said in the statement. “That is why these agreements, which ensure due process under the U.S. Constitution, are so essential to the safety of our homeland and the American people.”

Supreme Court ruling in
June

44580235.article_summary: 美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）发布了一份备忘录，允许在某些紧急情况下将移民驱逐到与其无联系的国家，即使这些移民可能面临迫害或酷刑风险。根据该备忘录，如果美国国务院认为目的地国家提供的外交保证可信，移民可以在六小时内被驱逐，无需进一步程序。通常情况下，移民会收到至少24小时的通知，并有机会与律师交谈。然而，批评者认为该政策无视法律和宪法要求，外交保证不充分且不透明，且时间过短，移民难以评估风险。国土安全部则称这些协议确保了正当程序，对国家安全至关重要。

data.title: LLM Inevitabilism
data.author: SwoopsFromAbove
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了与擅长辩论的人争论时的困境，以及如何通过控制对话框架来主导讨论。作者引用了一位擅长辩论的朋友和《监控资本主义时代》一书中的概念，特别是“不可避免论”（Inevitabilism）。这一观点认为某些技术未来必然会发生，人们只能适应而非质疑。作者以科技界名人关于人工智能（AI）的言论为例，指出这种框架实际上限制了对未来选择的讨论。作者强调，我们有权选择自己想要的未来，不应被“不可避免论”剥夺这种权利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）的未来发展及其在社会、技术和商业领域的不可避免性。

不同观点：
• 观点一（lsy）：LLMs作为一种新技术，难以被放弃，但目前尚未找到与其开发和维护成本相匹配的商业模式，且其能力趋于平庸，可能最终只会应用于特定场景，而不是像现在这样广泛且令人厌烦地使用。
• 观点二（keiferski）：现代人倾向于忽视千年以来的哲学和宗教思想，将技术视为不可避免的命运，这种“AI inevitabilism”类似于历史上的宿命论观念，是一种将自由和责任外包给技术的心理投射。
• 观点三（delichon）：LLMs的广泛应用是不可避免的，就像智能手机的普及一样。即使存在恐惧，技术的发展不可逆转。
• 观点四（Animats）：LLMs可能面临“LLM冬季”，因为它们不能被完全信任，企业会试图将错误责任转嫁给消费者。目前的使用体验可能并不理想。
• 观点五（tines）：担忧未来技术权力集中在少数人手中，社会失去自主能力，可能陷入迷信和黑暗。
• 观点六（mg）：LLMs的应用是不可避免的，正如互联网的发展一样。其在编程中的应用已经展示了巨大的时间节省潜力。
• 观点七（sircastor）：所谓“不可避免”是那些投入巨资开发和推广LLMs的人所宣扬的，目的是为了推动市场接受。
• 观点八（dasil003）：LLMs是一项新技术，但需要时间来充分理解和利用其能力。不应盲目接受科技CEO的炒作，而应由技术专家客观评估。
• 观点九（Workaccount2）：人们喜欢用自然语言交流，LLMs是计算技术发展的自然步骤，未来人们不再需要学习计算机逻辑语言。
• 观点十（pi_22by7）：“不可避免”是一种修辞策略，历史上有许多“不可避免”的未来最终崩溃，如何反驳这种论调而不显得幼稚或倒退是一个问题。
• 观点十一（trash_cat）：不可避免性与政治上的必然性类似，是一种剥夺人们主动权的语言策略。
• 观点十二（cdrini）：如何区分辩论技巧与真实思想，如何辨别好的论点与好的想法，这之间的界限并不总是清晰。
• 观点十三（JimmaDaRustla）：反对者错误地将AI的不可避免性视为一种辩论策略，而不是承认AI发展的必然性，IT行业需要正视LLMs的变革力量。
• 观点十四（ccortes）：当前许多初创公司都在做LLM相关项目，但这些项目缺乏创新，感觉非常平庸。

补充讨论：
• bloppe：LLMs的不可避免性依赖于其在多个领域超越人类能力的前提假设。如果这一假设不成立，所谓的不可避免性可能只是AI热潮中的一个梦想。

争议焦点：
• LLMs的未来发展是否真正不可避免，还是只是当前技术热潮和市场炒作的结果。
• 如何区分关于LLMs发展的真实论点与修辞策略，以及如何在技术发展中保持自主性和批判性。

44567857.article_content:
Have you ever argued with someone who is seriously good at debating? I have. It sucks.
You’re constantly thrown off-balance, responding to a point you didn’t expect to. You find yourself defending the weak edges of your argument, while the main thrust gets left behind in the back-and-forth, and you end up losing momentum, confidence, and ultimately, the argument.
One of my close friends won international debate competitions for fun while we were at university (he’s now a successful criminal barrister), and he told me that the only trick in the book, once you boil it all down, is to make sure the conversation is framed in your terms. Once that happens, it’s all over bar the shouting.
Earlier this year I read Professor Shoshana Zuboff’s fantastic book
The Age of Surveillance Capitalism
. I learned a lot from it (and I’m sure I’ll rave about it in more detail in other posts), including many new terms for phenomina that have long frustreated me.
Being able to put a name to something abstract allows you to more easily build an argument about it, explain the concept to strangers, and unify opposition to it. It’s a key success of Professor Zuboff’s book that it has introduced so many new terms to the lexicon.
The word that is relevant to this post is “Inevitabilism”.
People advancing an inevitabilist world view state that the future they perceive will inevitably come to pass. It follows, relatively straightforwardly, that the only sensible way to respond to this is to prepare as best you can for that future.
This is a
fantastic
framing method. Anyone who sees the future differently to you can be brushed aside as “ignoring reality”, and the only conversations worth engaging are those that
already accept your premise
.
“We are entering a world where we will learn to coexist with AI, not as its masters, but as its collaborators.” – Mark Zuckerberg
“AI is the new electricity.” – Andrew Ng
“AI will not replace humans, but those who use AI will replace those who don’t.” – Ginni Rometty
These are some big names in the tech world, all framing the conversation in a very specific way. Rather than
“is this the future you want?”
, the question is instead
“how will you adapt to this
inevitable
future?”
. Note also the threatening tone present, a healthy psychological undercurrent encouraging you to go with the flow, because you’d otherwise be messing with scary powers way beyond your understanding.
I’m not convinced that LLMs are the future. I’m certainly not convinced that they’re the future I want. But what I’m most certain of is that we have choices about what our future should look like, and how we choose to use machines to build it.
Don’t let inevitabilism frame the argument and take away your choice. Think about the future
you
want, and fight for it.
Technologies
AI
Related
Cull your dependencies
Should we welcome or fear the Metaverse?
Why am I doing this again?

data.title: Co-op (UK) boss confirms all 6.5M members had data stolen
data.author: mmarian
data.article_summary: Co-op首席执行官Shirine Khoury-Haq证实，4月网络攻击导致650万会员数据被盗，包括姓名、地址和联系方式，但没有财务或交易数据。她对此表示歉意，并强调对同事的影响令她个人非常难过。黑客已被清除，但数据已被泄露，公司已将信息交给当局。Co-op正与一家网络安全招聘公司合作，并计划通过Co-op Academies Trust开展试点项目，培养年轻网络人才走合法职业道路。此前，M&S和Harrods也遭遇类似攻击，英国国家犯罪局逮捕了四名与此案有关的嫌疑人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对信息被泄露的态度和责任归属

不同观点：
• 一方认为信息被泄露令人 devastated（ devastated 意为极度震惊和失望），对事件本身表示强烈的情感反应。这种观点更多关注信息泄露带来的后果和感受，代表发言为 "I'm devastated that information was taken"。
  
• 另一方则将责任归咎于信息管理者，认为他们允许了信息的泄露，因此也应该承担责任。这一观点强调信息保护的责任在于管理方，发言为 "How about devastated that you allowed it to be taken?"

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于信息泄露的责任归属问题。一方关注信息泄露的直接后果，表达情感上的强烈不满；另一方则认为管理者应对信息安全负责，强调管理不善的责任。
• 第二种观点隐含了对管理者失职的批评，指出他们本应采取措施防止信息泄露。
• 第一种观点主要表达了信息被泄露后的情感反应，而第二种观点则从事件的责任和预防角度提出了质疑。

44580340.article_content:
Media caption,
Watch: Co-op boss says immediate action was taken when the data breach was discovered
Joe Tidy
Cyber correspondent, BBC World Service
Imran Rahman-Jones
Technology reporter
Published
16 July 2025, 08:46 BST
Updated 2 hours ago
The chief executive of Co-op has confirmed that all 6.5 million of its members had their data stolen in a cyber-attack on the retailer in April.
"I'm devastated that information was taken. I'm also devastated by the impact that it took on our colleagues as well as they tried to contain all of this," Shirine Khoury-Haq told BBC Breakfast in her first public interview since the hack.
"There was no financial data, no transaction data but it was names and addresses and contact information that was lost," she added.
Ms Khoury-Haq said that she was "incredibly sorry" for the attack and that it was "personal" to her because of the impact that it had on her colleagues.
"Early on I met with our IT staff and they were in the midst of it. I will never forget the looks on their faces, trying to fight off these criminals," she said.
The hackers were removed from the systems but "could not erase what they did so we could monitor every mouse click," and Co-op was able to send that information to authorities.
But she added: "We know a lot of that information is out there anyway, but people will be worried and all members should be concerned."
Co-op runs on a membership scheme, where members are paid a share of the profits of the co-operative.
"It hurt my members, they took their data and it hurt our customers and that I do take personally," Ms Khoury-Haq said.
Co-op has not put a figure on how much the hack will cost them, but it says it is still working to restore back-end systems.
One of its responses to the hack is to partner with a cyber-security recruitment company.
The Hacking Games identifies young talent to channel their skills into legal careers.
"The research shows that if you offer these kids talent development opportunities and career opportunities, the vast majority of them will take the legitimate pathway," said its chief executive Fergus Hay.
It is planning a pilot programme with Co-op Academies Trust, which runs 38 schools in England.
What happened in the cyber-attacks?
Co-op was one of three retailers, alongside
Marks and Spencer
(M&S) and
Harrods
who were victims of cyber-attacks in spring this year.
Co-op
announced on 30 April
that it had been hacked, initially saying it would only have a "small impact" on its call centre and back office.
But days later, after being contacted by the alleged hackers, BBC News revealed that customer and employee data had been accessed.
Co-op
then admitted
the criminals had "accessed data relating to a significant number of our current and past members".
BBC News later discovered from the alleged attackers that the company
disconnected the internet
from IT networks in the nick of time to stop the hackers from deploying ransomware and so causing even more disruption.
M&S also had
customer data stolen
, and is still getting its systems back to normal
after huge disruption
which has cost it millions of pounds.
Last week, the National Crime Agency (NCA) said
four people had been arrested
in connection with the hacks on Co-op and M&S
These were a 20-year-old woman who was arrested in Staffordshire, and three males - aged between 17 and 19 - who were detained in London and the West Midlands.
They were apprehended on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences, blackmail, money laundering and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.
Additional reporting by Charlotte Edwards.

data.title: Thoughts on Motivation and My 40-Year Career
data.author: gpi
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一位作者对自我成长经历的反思，特别是从极度保守和宗教化的家庭背景中出走、追求独立的过程。作者15岁时离开家，凭借自学进入大学，正赶上互联网兴起和公立大学费用尚可负担的末期。为了完成学业，作者从事多份最低工资工作，同时因发现音乐专业的就业前景不佳，转向计算机和互联网领域。作者成长于一个严格信仰体系的家庭，尽管深爱父母，但这种信仰体系限制了其个人发展愿望，如对权力、金钱、自主性的追求。作者在青少年时期陷入严重抑郁，最终选择离开家庭，追寻更广阔的生活。这篇文章探讨了个人身份认同、家庭关系以及逃离限制性环境的复杂情感。

44580411.article_content:
I’ve never published an essay quite like this. I’ve written about my life before, reams of stuff actually, because that’s how I process what I think, but never for public consumption.
I’ve been pushing myself to write more lately because my co-authors and I have a whole fucking book to write between now and October. After ten years, you’d think this would be getting easier, not harder.
There’s something about putting out such memoiristic material that feels uncomfortably feminine to me. (Wow,
ok
.) I want to be known for my work, not for having a dramatic personal life. I love my family and don’t want to put them on display for the world to judge. And I never want the people I care about to feel like I am mining their experiences for clicks and content, whether that’s my family or my coworkers.
Many of the writing exercises I’ve been doing lately have ended up pulling on threads from my backstory, and the reason I haven’t published them is because I find myself thinking, “this won’t make any sense to people unless they know where I’m coming from.”
So hey, fuck it, let’s do this.
I went to college at the luckiest time
I left home when I was 15 years old. I left like a bottle rocket taking off – messy, explosive, a trail of destruction in my wake, and with absolutely zero targeting mechanisms.
It tells you a lot about how sheltered I was that the only place I could think of to go was university. I had never watched TV or been to a sports game or listened to popular music. I had never been to a doctor, I was quite unvaccinated.
I grew up in the backwoods of Idaho, the oldest of six, all of us homeschooled. I would go for weeks without seeing anyone other than my family. The only way to pass the time was by reading books or playing piano, so I did quite a lot of both. I called up the University of Idaho, asked for an admissions packet, hand wrote myself a transcript and gave myself all As, drove up and auditioned for the music department, and was offered a partial ride scholarship for classical piano performance.
I told my parents I was leaving, with or without their blessing or financial support. I left with neither.
My timing turned out to be flawless. I arrived on the cusp of the Internet age – they were wiring dorms for ethernet the year I enrolled. Maybe even more important, I arrived in the final, fading glory years of affordable state universities.
I worked multiple minimum wage jobs to put myself through school; day care, front desk, laundry, night audit. It was grueling, round the clock labor, but it was possible, if you were stubborn enough. I didn’t have a Social Security number (long story), I wasn’t old enough to take out loans, I couldn’t get financial aid because my parents didn’t file income taxes (again, long story). There was no help coming, I sank or I swam.
I found computers and the Internet around the same time as it dawned on me that everybody who studied music seemed to end up poor as an adult. I grew up too poor to buy canned vegetables or new underwear; we were like an 1800s family, growing our food, making our clothes, hand-me-downs til they fell apart.
Fuck being poor. Fuck it so hard. I was out.
I lost my music scholarship, but I started building websites and running systems for the university, then for local businesses. I dropped out and took a job in San Francisco. I went back, abortively; I dropped out again.
By the time I was 20 I was back in SF for good, making a salary five times what my father had made.
I grew up with a very coherent belief system that did not work for me
A lot of young people who flee their fundamentalist upbringing do so because they were abused and/or lost their faith, usually due to the hypocrisy of their leaders. Not me. I left home still believing the whole package – that evolution was a fraud, that the earth was created in seven days, that woman was created from Adam’s rib to be a submissive helpmate for their husband, that birth control was a sin, that anyone who believed differently was going to hell.
My parents loved us deeply and unshakably, and they were not hypocrites. In the places I grew up, the people who believed in God and went to church and lived a certain way were the ones who had their shit together, and the people who believed differently had broken lives. Reality seemed to confirm the truth of all we were taught, no matter how outlandish it sounds.
So I fully believed it was all true. I also knew it
did not work
for me
. I did not want a small life. I did not want to be the support system behind some godly dude. I wanted power, money, status, fame, autonomy, success. I wanted to leave a crater in the world.
I was not a rebellious child, believe it or not. I loved my parents and wanted to make them proud. But as I entered my teens, I became severely depressed, and turned inward and hurt myself in all the ways young people do.
I left because staying there was killing me, and ultimately, I think my parents let me go because they saw it too.

44580765.article_content:
The breakthrough proof bringing mathematics closer to a grand unified theory
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
Illustration: Andy Gilmore
One of the biggest stories in science is quietly playing out in the world of abstract mathematics. Over the course of last year, researchers fulfilled a decades-old dream when they unveiled a proof of the geometric Langlands conjecture — a key piece of a group of interconnected problems called the Langlands programme. The proof — a gargantuan effort — validates the intricate and far-reaching Langlands programme, which is often hailed as the grand unified theory of mathematics but remains largely unproven. Yet the work’s true impact might lie not in what it settles, but in the new avenues of inquiry it reveals.
“It’s a huge triumph. But rather than closing a door, this proof throws open a dozen others,” says David Ben-Zvi at the University of Texas at Austin, who was not involved with the work.
‘Mind blowing’: quantum computer untangles the mathematics of knots
Proving the geometric Langlands conjecture has long been considered one of the deepest and most enigmatic pursuits in modern mathematics. Ultimately, it took a team of nine mathematicians to crack the problem, in a series of five papers spanning almost 1,000 pages
1
–
5
. The group was led by Dennis Gaitsgory at the Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in Bonn, Germany, and Sam Raskin at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, who completed his PhD with Gaitsgory in 2014.
The magnitude of their accomplishment was quickly recognized by the mathematical community: in April,
Gaitsgory received the US$3-million Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics
, and Raskin was awarded a New Horizons prize for promising early-career mathematicians. Like many landmark results in mathematics, the proof promises to forge bridges between different areas, allowing the tools of one domain to tackle intractable problems in another. All told, it’s a heady time for researchers in these fields.
“It gives us the strongest evidence yet that something we’ve believed in for decades is true,” says Ben-Zvi. “Now we can finally ask: what does it really mean?”
The hole story
The Langlands programme traces its origins back 60 years, to the work of a young Canadian mathematician named
Robert Langlands
, who set out his vision in a handwritten letter to the
leading mathematician André Weil
. Over the decades, the programme attracted increasing attention from mathematicians, who marvelled at how all-encompassing it was. It was that feature that led Edward Frenkel at the University of California, Berkeley,
who has made key contributions to the geometric side
, to call it the grand unified theory of mathematics.
Langlands’ aim was to connect two very separate major branches of mathematics — number theory (the study of integers) and harmonic analysis (the study of how complicated signals or functions break down into simple waves). A special case of the Langlands programme is the epic proof that Andrew Wiles published, in 1995, of
Fermat’s last theorem
— that no three positive integers

and

satisfy the equation

Robert Langlands discussed his ideas in a letter to André Weil in 1967. On the cover page to the letter (left), Langlands says, “If you are willing to read it as pure speculation I would appreciate that; if not — I am sure you have a waste basket handy.”
Credit: Institute for Advanced Study (Princeton, N.J.) Shelby White and Leon Levy Archives Center
The geometric Langlands conjecture was first developed in the 1980s by Vladimir Drinfeld, then at the B. Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering in Kharkiv, Ukraine. Like the original or arithmetic form of the Langlands conjecture, the geometric conjecture also makes a type of connection: it suggests a correspondence between two different sets of mathematical objects. Although the fields linked by the arithmetic form of Langlands are separate mathematical ‘worlds’, the differences between the two sides of the geometric conjecture are not so pronounced. Both concern properties of Riemann surfaces, which are ‘complex manifolds’ — structures with coordinates that are complex numbers (with real and imaginary parts). These manifolds can take the form of spheres, doughnuts or pretzel-like shapes with two or more holes.
Many mathematicians strongly suspect that the ‘closeness’ of the two sides means the proof of the geometric Langlands conjecture could eventually offer some traction for furthering the arithmetic version, in which the relationships are more mysterious. “To truly understand the Langlands correspondence, we have to realize that the ‘two worlds’ in it are not that different — rather, they are two facets of one and the same world,” says Frenkel. “Seeing this unity requires a new vision, a new understanding. data.title: Apple's MLX adding CUDA support
data.author: nsagent
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了在MLX项目中添加CUDA后端的进展。贡献者zcbenz正在进行一个 pull request (PR)，目标是将CUDA后端整合到MLX中，目前该功能还在开发中，但教程示例已经可以运行。添加CUDA后端的主要原因包括CUDA支持统一内存，并且NVIDIA硬件广泛用于学术和大规模计算，这将改善开发者在本地编写和测试代码后部署到超级计算机的体验。此外，文章还提到有计划添加ROCm支持，并讨论了如何同时管理CUDA和ROCm后端的两种可能模式。该工作由Apple赞助。PR目前还在频繁更新中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MLX与CUDA的兼容性及其在不同平台（尤其是Apple Silicon和CUDA硬件）上的应用

不同观点：
• **[lukev]的观点**：MLX程序可以利用CUDA芯片，但CUDA程序不能直接在Apple Silicon上运行，因为这可能涉及侵犯NVIDIA的版权。
• **[nxobject]的观点**：MLX的补丁增加了对Linux平台上CUDA 12和Volta及以上版本的支持，暗示CUDA在不同平台上的支持扩展。
• **[mattfrommars]的观点**：到2025年，CUDA尚未实现“编写一次，随处运行”的愿景，学术界和公司仍在编写专有代码，这类似于继续使用Adobe Flash或Microsoft Silverlight。

补充讨论：
• **[paulirish]的观点**：MLX的开发者具有很高的声望（如创建Electron的zcbenz），增加了项目的可信度。
• **[zdw]的观点**：MLX使用统一内存架构（UMA），这对所有UMA APU是有趣的，但对于独立GPU可能需要不同的方法。CUDA支持UMA API并自动处理必要的复制操作。
• **[neurostimulant]的观点**：能够在Mac上编写和测试代码，然后部署到超级计算机上，会带来良好的开发体验。MLX目前可以在Linux上使用，但仅支持Python 3.12版本。
• **[dnchdnd]的观点**：MLX的开发者似乎并不正式隶属于Apple，这引发了Apple是否在秘密支持该项目的猜测。
• **[numpad0]的观点**：MLX添加CUDA后端是为了让MLX代码在x86和GeForce硬件上编译和运行，而不是相反。
• **[MuffinFlavored]的观点**：MLX似乎实现了“编写一次，随处使用”的理念，可以在Linux CUDA和Apple Silicon/Metal上运行。
• **[albertzeyer]的观点**：CUDA的统一内存功能如何在Apple Silicon和NVIDIA硬件上工作是一个值得关注的问题，特别是在CPU和GPU之间内存共享和复制操作方面。
• **[Abishek_Muthian]的观点**：MLX在Apple Silicon上的表现令人印象深刻，希望Apple Silicon能成为NVIDIA芯片的有力竞争者，但也担心CUDA支持可能是一种“拥抱、扩展和消灭”策略。
• **[sciencesama]的观点**：Apple计划使用M系列芯片构建数据中心，用于应用程序开发、测试和托管外部服务。
• **[qwertox]的观点**：如果Apple支持NVIDIA卡，它将成为开发者的首选解决方案。
• **[benreesman]的观点**：Strix Halo的性能与中高端EC2和GCE实例相比具有竞争力，但ROCm尚未完全支持。如果CUDA能在Apple设备上完美运行，将极大提升其吸引力。
• **[neuroelectron]的观点**：为fp8内核命名为“cutlass”可以提高50%的性能。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于MLX和CUDA之间的兼容性以及Apple Silicon和NVIDIA硬件之间的支持关系。具体而言，是否能在Apple Silicon上直接运行CUDA程序，以及Apple是否在秘密支持MLX项目，是讨论的核心问题。

总结：
评论主要围绕MLX和CUDA的兼容性及其在不同硬件平台上的应用展开。讨论涉及技术细节如统一内存架构、不同平台的支持情况以及对未来开发环境的展望。同时，Apple是否在背后支持MLX项目也是讨论的热点。

This PR is an ongoing effort to add a CUDA backend to MLX, very little things work now but you can run the tutorial example already.
To build and test:
$
cmake
.
-Bbuild -DMLX_BUILD_CUDA=ON -DMLX_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
$
cmake --build build -j 16
$
./build/examples/cpp/tutorial
array([[2, 3],
[4, 5]], dtype=float32)
array([[1, 1],
[1, 1]], dtype=float32)
For development I usually use:
$
cmake
.
-Bbuild -DMLX_BUILD_CUDA=ON -DMLX_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -GNinja
Only tested on a Ubuntu 22.04 with CUDA 11.6, in theory other environments can also work but there are no testings.
This PR is not updated frequently, if anyone is interested in the realtime development, please check
my forked repo
.
There are mainly 2 reasons for a CUDA backend:
CUDA supports unified memory. Including hardware support in some devices, and software support for devices without hardware unified memory.
NVIDIA hardware is widely used for academic and massive computations. Being able to write/test code locally on a Mac and then deploy to super computers would make a good developer experience.
This work is sponsored by Apple.

44565668.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了在MLX项目中添加CUDA后端的进展。贡献者zcbenz正在进行一个 pull request (PR)，目标是将CUDA后端整合到MLX中，目前该功能还在开发中，但教程示例已经可以运行。添加CUDA后端的主要原因包括CUDA支持统一内存，并且NVIDIA硬件广泛用于学术和大规模计算，这将改善开发者在本地编写和测试代码后部署到超级计算机的体验。此外，文章还提到有计划添加ROCm支持，并讨论了如何同时管理CUDA和ROCm后端的两种可能模式。该工作由Apple赞助。PR目前还在频繁更新中。

data.title: Japanese grandparents create life-size Totoro with bus stop for grandkids (2020)
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 日本宫崎县高畠町的一对七旬老人为了给孙子们带来快乐，亲手制作了一个等身大的龙猫雕像，重现了电影《龙猫》中的经典场景。他们运用传统灰泥技术和混凝土，精心雕刻出龙猫的圆润身形和独特表情，并在雕像旁边设置了电影中的公交站标志。这个项目不仅让他们的孙子们非常开心，还吸引了世界各地的龙猫粉丝前来参观拍照。雕像旁还提供电影中的红色雨伞供游客使用。通过这对夫妇的努力，这个小小的村庄成为了龙猫迷和怀旧者新的观光打卡点。

Home

Japanese Grandparents Create Life-Size Totoro With Bus Stop For Their Grandkids
By
Sonya Harris
on August 19, 2020
Photo:
ikeimage
Totoro is a hallmark character created by
Studio Ghibli
, Japan's beloved animation studio. The plump bodied, wide smiling magical creature’s most iconic image is that of him waiting for an unusual bus in the rain. The magic of that scene (featured in the 1988 film
My Neighbor Totoro)
has been a spark of nostalgia, imagination, and inspiration for a variety of creatives. Such is the case for a pair of grandparents in Takaharu, Miyazaki Prefecture, Japan. The couple—who is in their 70s—decided to recreate the magic of the film by designing a Totoro replica for their grandchildren.
The project was handmade and demonstrated the couple’s exceptional skill in carpentry and their impeccable attention to detail. By using some traditional plastering techniques, the barrel-like frame for the future statue was constructed first. This was followed by layers of concrete and a lengthy process of sculpting. Bricks were then added to help create the signature plumpness of the magical gray beast’s frame. Even more concrete was layered on and with careful sculpting, the memorable, bold eyes and whiskers started to emerge. The couple finished up the project by adding a brick and gravel path around the structure and placed the iconic bus stop sign.
The statue—which towers over children and adults alike—was not only a big hit with the grandkids but is currently drawing in adoring Totoro fans from far and wide to the small town. The couple also provides the signature red umbrella from the film for any visiting photographers and selfie lovers. Thanks to the love and vision of this elderly couple, long time Totoro fans and magic seekers alike have another pit stop, when it comes to sightseeing and nostalgia.
This grandfather in Japan carefully built the frame of what would soon be a very large statue.
Along with his wife, he put time and effort into creating this giant sculpture of the famed Totoro.
The lengthy process required concrete, careful sculpting, and bricks.
The grandparents were able to complete Totoro's whimsical face with some painting and more sculpting to make sure every detail was captured.
In the end, they were ready for a family photo with a very happy grandchild!
Their hard work has made a lot more than their grandkids happy, though. Totoro fans from all around the world now visit this village to see the sculpture and take a picture with it.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Elo和Bradley-Terry排序算法实现及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• scoresmoke分享了一个自研的Elo和Bradley-Terry算法的实现，该实现具有Rust核心、Python绑定、100%测试覆盖率和良好的API。
• david_shi认为此实现让人联想到PageRank的直觉背后的原理。
• Alex3917提问为何使用传统的Elo而不是不假设结果分布的Elo变种，例如whole_history_rating。
• pbhjpbhj讨论了在文档检索中使用配对方法的可能性，并询问是否有人研究过在不同概念层次上改进检索的机器学习方法。
• ashwindharne分享了内部使用现成模型进行重新排序和过滤的经验，并表示这种方法效果良好。

补充讨论：
• Neywiny提到其论文中使用2AFC排序而不是Elo，并提供了代码和会议摘要链接。
• seanhunter和bbstats提醒大家Elo是发明者的名字，而不是缩写。
• etk934提问使用MSE训练的重新排序器是否比使用InfoNCE的更校准，以及在RAG应用中重新排序评分阈值是否更有用。
• mkaszkowiak询问该模型支持的语言和多语言基准测试情况。
• rahulnair23提到其在ACL 2024上的论文，提供了关于LLM排名的研究链接。
• yalok关注运行重新排序器带来的额外延迟。
• esafak建议将项目标题改为"Improving ranking..."并表示对使用sentence_transformers的喜爱。
• sippeangelo提醒scoresmoke忘记在末尾链接到evals。

争议焦点：
• 是否应使用传统的Elo或其不假设结果分布的变种（如whole_history_rating）以提高排序效果。

data.title: Pgactive: Postgres active-active replication extension
data.author: ForHackernews
data.article_summary: **pgactive** 是一个 PostgreSQL 扩展，用于实现 **active-active（双活）数据库复制。这种复制方式允许多个数据库实例同时接受写入操作，并相互复制数据，适用于多区域高可用性、减少写入延迟、蓝绿部署等场景。与传统的 active-standby 模式不同，active-active 没有单一的数据来源，因此需要处理数据冲突和复制延迟等问题。该项目利用 PostgreSQL 的逻辑复制功能，并通过扩展增强其对双活复制的支持。项目基于 Apache-2.0 许可证，目前有 426 个星标和 19 个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres的逻辑复制、冲突解决机制、本地可写读副本的实现以及AWS使用场景分析

不同观点：
• [eatonphil] 提供了BDR和pglogical的演变历史。他指出BDR1是开源的，pgactive基于BDR1，而BDR2是闭源且被废弃的。pglogical有多个版本，其中v1被合并到Postgres 10中，之后2nd Quadrant开发了pglogical v2和v3以及BDR v3（闭源），最终合并为BDR v4，后来更名为Postgres Distributed (PGD)。2nd Quadrant被EDB收购，EDB刚刚发布了PGD v6。

• [zknill] 认为pgactive使用Postgres逻辑复制在实例间共享更改，采用基于时间戳的“最后写入为准”冲突解决机制，并将冲突记录到特殊表中以便后续处理。

• [nico] 提出了一种关于“本地可写读副本”的需求，即副本可以从主数据库获取数据但不回传本地更改。他提到目前的解决方案通常是通过脚本定期获取数据快照，但指出索引构建可能耗时较长。

• [ahachete] 强调“冲突解决”实际上是“丢弃已提交数据”，并建议要么在架构上避免写冲突，要么使用像Yugabyte这样的纯分布式数据库。

• [everfrustrated] 对AWS为何开发pgactive感到困惑，指出AWS的RDS和Aurora使用不同的复制技术，猜测可能与DMS有关。

• [iotapi322] 基于实际操作经验，表示不会使用这种插件，担心其稳定性和对生产环境的影响。

• [dang] 提到相关讨论链接，但没有详细观点。

• [dangoodmanUT] 指出pgactive的异步特性可能导致事务隔离问题。

• [ltbarcly3] 警告除非非常了解该技术，否则不应使用，强调这并不是提升性能或可扩展性的通用方法。

补充讨论：
• pgactive的冲突解决机制和其“最后写入为准”策略的有效性和风险是讨论的焦点。
• 对AWS使用场景的猜测和疑惑反映了用户对实际应用背景的不明确。
• 关于本地可写读副本的讨论提出了实际应用中的需求和现有解决方案的局限性。
• 对pgactive的实际操作稳定性存在担忧，特别是在生产环境中的使用。
• 技术实现的异步特性和事务隔离问题也被提及，显示出用户对数据一致性和可靠性的关注。

Active-active Replication Extension for PostgreSQL (pgactive)
pgactive is a PostgreSQL replication extension for creating an active-active database.
Documentation
Overview
Security
License
Overview
Database replication is a method that copies changes between databases instances, and is a key component for use cases like high availability, reducing latency between an application and its source data, moving data between systems such as production and test, infrastructure migration, and others. Relational databases such as PostgreSQL typically support an active-standby model of replication, where one database instance accepts changes and makes them available to one or more read-only databases. Because changes in an active-standby cluster can only occur on a single instance, it’s more straightforward to build applications that work with this deployment topology because there is a single source of truth that contains all of the latest changes.
Sometimes it’s preferable to have a database cluster that uses an active-active replication topology, where it’s possible to write data on multiple instances in the same cluster. In an asynchronous active-active replication deployment, multiple databases in a cluster can accept changes and replicate them to other databases, but this means the database cluster doesn’t have a single source of truth. Use cases for this include running a Multi-Region high availability database cluster, reducing write latency between applications and databases, performing blue/green updates of applications, and migrating data between systems that must both be writable. Applications that work with active-active database clusters must be designed to handle situations that occur in this deployment topology, including conflicting changes, replication lag, and the lack of certain convenient database features such as incremental integer sequences.
A fundamental component of active-active replication is logical replication. Logical replication uses a data format that allows external systems to interpret changes before applying them to a target database. This lets the target system perform additional actions, such as detecting and resolving write conflicts or converting the statement into something that is supported in the target database software. PostgreSQL added native support for logical replication in PostgreSQL 10 in 2017, but still requires additional features to fully support an active-active replication topology. PostgreSQL’s design makes it possible to build the necessary components for supporting active-active replication in an extension while the development community continues to add it into the upstream project.

44580257.article_summary: **pgactive** 是一个 PostgreSQL 扩展，用于实现 **active-active（双活）数据库复制。这种复制方式允许多个数据库实例同时接受写入操作，并相互复制数据，适用于多区域高可用性、减少写入延迟、蓝绿部署等场景。与传统的 active-standby 模式不同，active-active 没有单一的数据来源，因此需要处理数据冲突和复制延迟等问题。该项目利用 PostgreSQL 的逻辑复制功能，并通过扩展增强其对双活复制的支持。项目基于 Apache-2.0 许可证，目前有 426 个星标和 19 个分支。

data.author: gjvc
data.article_summary: cppyy 是一个自动的 Python-C++ 绑定生成工具，能够在运行时实现 Python 与 C++ 的互调，支持跨语言调用、延迟加载、模板实例化、异常映射等功能。它基于 C++ 解释器 Cling，无需语言扩展或手写代码，支持大型 C++ 项目，并能无缝集成如 Boost 等复杂 C++ 库。cppyy 适用于 CPython 和 PyPy，具备高性能，支持 STL、回调和跨继承等特性，简化了 C++ 库在 Python 中的使用。通过预编译头文件和动态加载等技术，cppyy 可以处理包含大量类和代码的 C++ 项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cppyy 作为 Python 和 C++ 结合的工具，其功能、性能及实际应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• [rich_sasha] 认为 Cppyy 类似于已经废弃的 scipy.weave，可以结合 C++ 和 Python。他关注 Cppyy 是否能替代 scipy.weave，尤其是性能方面是否能超越 Numba 和 Cython。他指出 Cppyy 通过 Cling 解释 C++ 而不是生成真正的二进制文件，并质疑其在 CPython3 上的性能表现。虽然找到了一些基准测试，但这些测试并没有直接对比 Python 实现。

• [ashvardanian] 提供了一个使用 Cppyy 的实际用例，展示如何通过 Cppyy 结合 C++ 内核与 Python 进行实验，还提到了 Numba 和 PeachPy 等其他工具，展示了 Cppyy 在实际项目中的应用场景。

• [f1shy] 提出了 Cppyy 与 LLM（大型语言模型）在“AI 编程”中的对比，表示自己在使用 Cppyy 时得到了不错的效果，询问其他人的使用体验。

• [dang] 提供了一个相关的讨论链接，指向 2019 年关于 Cppyy 的讨论，引导读者参考之前的讨论内容。

• [actinium226] 关注实际应用中的分发问题，担心如果在项目中使用 Cppyy 并打包成 pip 包，用户是否需要自行安装 C++ 编译器，或者 Cppyy 是否自带编译器。

• [wslh] 推荐了 SWIG 作为另一种支持多种编程语言的绑定工具，暗示 SWIG 可能是 Cppyy 的一种替代方案。

补充讨论：
• [bogeholm] 对项目名称进行了幽默评论，没有涉及技术讨论。

争议焦点：
• Cppyy 是否真正能替代 scipy.weave，尤其是在性能和实用性方面。
• Cppyy 在实际项目分发中的可行性，特别是对用户环境的要求。

基准测试和性能对比是讨论的核心，尤其是对 Cppyy 在 CPython3 上的性能表现缺乏明确的答案。

cppyy: Automatic Python-C++ bindings

cppyy is an automatic, run-time, Python-C++ bindings generator, for calling
C++ from Python and Python from C++.
Run-time generation enables detailed specialization for higher performance,
lazy loading for reduced memory use in large scale projects, Python-side
cross-inheritance and callbacks for working with C++ frameworks, run-time
template instantiation, automatic object downcasting, exception mapping, and
interactive exploration of C++ libraries.
cppyy delivers this without any language extensions, intermediate languages,
or the need for boiler-plate hand-written code.

PyHPC’16 paper

data.title: Pascal's Scams (2012)
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 文章警告人们提防“帕斯卡骗局”：即那些让人关注极不可能发生但后果重大的事件的运动或信仰体系。这类骗局利用简单的期望值计算，诱导人们投入巨大努力去追求极小概率的高回报。文章指出这类信仰有三大问题：首先，由于证据不足，难以区分极小概率和极微小概率事件；其次，可能后果的多样性和程度高度不确定；最后，这类命题往往无法通过实验验证，导致信息无法改善。文章建议，面对低概率高风险假设时，应避免仅依赖定量分析，而需结合定性、逻辑和因果分析，并在无法获取足够信息时停止无谓的担忧或幻想。简言之，应务实对待不确定性，避免被“帕斯卡骗局”误导。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“低概率高影响事件的认知偏差”及其在不同场景中的表现和应用的讨论，包括实际生活决策、哲学思考、有效利他主义和商业推销等。

不同观点：
• **低概率事件的忽视**：superb-owl 提出人们往往忽略低概率高影响事件，比如醉驾或不系安全带，因为这些事件“可能”没事。他通过朋友因侥幸心理被罚款的例子说明这一点。

• **帕斯卡的赌注及其变种**：praptak 提到帕斯卡的赌注有一个变种，称为“帕斯卡的劫掠”（Pascal's mugging），概念类似，但名称不同。b450 进一步指出帕斯卡的推理可以应用于无限可能的灾难，比如外星人入侵，这种推理如果不加限制会让人陷入瘫痪。

• **有效利他主义的应用**：munchler 认为有效利他主义在讨论远未来数万亿人类福祉时犯了类似的错误，强调对遥远未来的投入可能忽视了当前的现实问题。empath75 补充说，理性主义者和有效利他主义者经常陷入这种思维，例如Roko's Basilisk的思想实验，赋予某些结果无限的负值或正值，导致不理性的决策。

• **商业销售中的应用**：alach11 提到在商业推销中，销售人员常使用类似的策略，强调通过服务可以节省大量成本，诱导客户做出购买决策。

• **哲学与怀疑主义**：BigChemical 指出帕斯卡的赌注不仅仅是关于概率，更是关于讲故事和无限回报的诱惑，这种诱惑在今天的加密货币和高风险投资中依然存在。他强调怀疑主义是最好的防御。

补充讨论：
